#877. Tosin Adarabioyo: ‘No one can chat s*** about Cole Palmer’

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Interview: Adarabioyo, speaking at the launch of his trading card shop, issued a passionate defence of his former Chelsea team-mate Palmer amid criticism of his attitude

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Tosin Adarabioyo has leapt to the defence of former Chelsea team-mate Cole Palmer amid criticism of the Englishman’s attitude.

Palmer came under fire for a viral interaction with Joao Pedro after Chelsea’s bruising 4-1 thrashing by Leeds last weekend, brushing off the Brazilian after opting not to acknowledge the home fans who booed the team at full-time.

The 24-year-old is going through a difficult patch at the moment, having been left out of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad again for the November internationals after the German manager claimed “he misses too opportunities to impress”.

This led to questions over Palmer’s commitment to the England cause, something club team-mate Morgan Rogers emphatically refuted as “nonsense” and “a lie”.

And Tosin, who moved to from Chelsea to rivals Tottenham in the summer, has now become the latest to publicly back Palmer, with whom he shared two seasons at Stamford Bridge.

“No one can chat s*** about Cole,” Tosin said.

“For me, he's one of the best players I've ever seen. You can say what you want. Honestly, you guys can say what you want. He's a top level player. He will continue to get better.”

Asked whether he was surprised about Palmer’s omission from the England squad, he replied: “Yeah, for sure. Of course, I'm surprised. For me, he's the best No 10 in the Premier League.”

Tosin also echoed Rogers’ sentiment in regards to doubts over Palmer’s hunger to play for the Three Lions, with the Chelsea forward struggling to get back in favour with Tuchel after missing out on the World Cup, before his return to the international fold in September was swiftly curtailed by injury.

“False, false, false,” Tosin added. “I know Cole's dreams, his aspirations. So, yeah, it's completely false.”

While Tosin will passionately defend Palmer against his critics, this doesn’t spare the Chelsea man of a friendly jibe, especially in the wake of Tottenham’s first win at Stamford Bridge in eight years last month.

Palmer was sent off in the 2-0 defeat to their fierce rivals and Tosin, who missed the match through injury, was sure to savour the triumph at his mate’s expense.

Asked if the pair shared some post-match banter, Tosin laughed: “Cole's my guy, man - yeah, of course. But I'll keep that secret.”

Palmer was among a number of Tosin’s team-mates, past and present, supporting him at the launch of his trading card shop, Card Cop, in London. The retail space in Borough Yards will open to the public on Thursday 26 November.

The Spurs defender, who is an avid collector, is joined by the likes of former Blues team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill, as well as West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, in investing in the business.

Along with the investors, Chelsea’s contingent at the launch party included Rogers, Emmanuel Emegha and Jamie Gittens, while the likes of Dominic Solanke, Micky van de Ven, Archie Gray and Ben Davies came down to support their relatively new Spurs colleague.

“It’s a testament to what we're like as a team,” Tosin said. “We're all very close and very supportive of each other. The boys didn't have to turn up today, but they did. It's amazing. I'm very thankful to them.”

After a dire start to the season, feeling the hangover of their near-miss with relegation last term, Spurs have finally found their groove under Roberto De Zerbi and are now just one point off Chelsea after four wins in five.

Tosin puts the uptick in form down to the team’s Marbella training camp during the first international break of the season, which was crucial in forming a bond within the team.

“It's our trip to Marbella,” he said. “We had a great time. We bonded together. We learned a lot about each other, and we're all striving to put this club where we think it belongs.”

#876. Are Manchester City living through their David Moyes era?

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

It might get worse before it gets better for Manchester City fans

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Never be the man after ‘the man’, the saying goes. Football history is stippled with cautionary tales of managers who followed an all-time great, only to discover that they were doomed from the very beginning.

Manchester City have stumbled through a bruising autumn under Enzo Maresca, uncharacteristically so. It is impossible not to wonder if the Etihad Stadium is experiencing its very own version of Manchester United's 2013/14.

For a decade, Pep Guardiola bent English football to his will, turning Man City into a relentless, trophy-winning machine. Succeeding a figure who loomed so large over the east side of Manchester was never going to be straightforward. Few, though, expected the drop-off to feel quite so jarring, or quite so familiar.

David Moyes arrived at Old Trafford in 2013 tasked with prolonging Sir Alex Ferguson’s dynasty, meanwhile Maresca was handed a three-year contract this summer to keep Guardiola’s juggernaut in motion. Four months into the job, the steering wheel is juddering uncomfortably.

Man City’s recent results make for grim reading compared to the standards set over the last 10 years. A 3-1 defeat away at Nottingham Forest earlier this month was double-take worthy, before Saturday’s 1-1 home draw with Fulham - rescued only by an Elliot Anderson volley - saw them lose yet more ground in the Premier League title race.

On Tuesday night in the Champions League, Man City needed an 86th-minute Rayan Cherki strike just to salvage a 2-2 draw at home to Napoli, currently eighth in Serie A and 14 points off the pace.

Ahead of Sunday’s trip to league leaders Arsenal, Maresca's men look a shadow of the team that so recently struck fear into the Gunners' title hopes.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Predictably, the question of Maresca’s future has already begun to take on more of a 'when rather than if' feel. Reports emerged this week suggesting the Italian is fighting to save his job barely a third of the way into his debut Etihad campaign. Sack talk at Manchester City circulating at all, never mind in November, speaks volumes about how rapidly things have changed.

There are parallels between Man City’s recent slump and Moyes’ 10-month spell across town, too. Like Moyes, Maresca inherited a squad undergoing significant churn after an era of dominance.

To bridge that gap, City made a throng of big summer purchases, bringing in additions such as Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez, Iliman Ndiaye and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Much like Moyes’ integration of Marouane Fellaini and Juan Mata into a fading champion side, Maresca’s new-look Man City feels disjointed - caught between Guardiola’s positional automatisms and a new manager’s attempt to stamp his own authority on the dressing room.

That disconnect quickly becomes apparent when the team aren't getting results, breeding doubt among players accustomed to certainty and success. All of which begs the question: was Maresca always doomed to fail?

Following Guardiola was always going to be an exercise in managing impossible expectations while rebuilding in real time. Perhaps the Etihad hierarchy believed their structure would insulate Guardiola’s successor from the same sort of post-Ferguson collapse that swallowed Moyes' efforts - which in hindsight weren't all that bad. Perhaps there is a lesson there for Man City chiefs to heed.

Joe joined FourFourTwo as senior digital writer in July 2025 after five years covering Leeds United in the Championship and Premier League. Joe's 'Mastermind' specialist subject is 2000s-era Newcastle United having had a season ticket at St. James' Park for 10 years before relocating to Leeds and later London. Joe takes a keen interest in youth football, covering PL2, U21 Euros, as well as U20 and U17 World Cups in the past, in addition to hosting the industry-leading football recruitment-focused SCOUTED podcast. He is also one of the lucky few to have 'hit top bins' as a contestant on Soccer AM. It wasn't a shin-roller.

#875. One person had a worse night than United keeper – the wretched referee

By the end of another utterly chaotic 90 minutes in the Manchester United soap opera, there was only one person who had endured a worse night than Senne Lammens.

Watching this game back will make for grim viewing for the United goalkeeper who, having been one of the club’s shining lights last season, is steadily becoming enveloped in a crisis of his own in this most torrid of campaigns.

But Roberto Rosetti, Uefa’s chief refereeing officer, might also want to sit Szymon Marciniak down after this and pick over the Polish official’s own nightmare performance. Marciniak denied United two goals, both of which should have stood, and in doing so ended up shining an even more brutal lens on Lammens’s calamitous display.

United’s Belgian goalkeeper was responsible for both of Sporting’s goals. He needlessly conceded a penalty in the first half, after a rush of blood to the head, that was converted by Luis Suárez, just 75 seconds after he had saved a spot-kick from the Sporting striker.

United had recovered from those bewildering few minutes to lead early in the second half, courtesy of two goals from captain Bruno Fernandes against his old club.

But, 10 minutes from time, Lammens committed the kind of howler that becomes worse and worse with every viewing. In doing so, he handed Sporting an equaliser and ensured United remain without an away win this season.

Lammens could have come to meet Iván Fresneda’s cross 100 times and probably dropped the ball only once. It was his and United’s misfortune that it should happen here. Suárez could barely believe his luck, although his finish was still accomplished, an acrobatic overhead kick from close range.

Senne Lammens with a gift for Luis Suárez to equalise for Sporting 🤯 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/kOQ6HImlVc

One of the stars of last season for United, Lammens is being dragged down with the rest of them this time around. He had looked hesitant from the moment he was almost caught dealing with a back-pass by Suárez in the opening minutes. It set the tone for what was to come.

As if Mauricio Pochettino did not already have enough on his plate, United’s new head coach now has a goalkeeper problem.

Of course, this would not have been as costly a night for Lammens had Marciniak not made such a mess of things himself. United may have been their own worst enemies again, but there was little doubting Sporting were given a helping hand here by some truly wretched refereeing.

The worst of it was the denial of a perfectly legitimate equaliser late in the first half after Youri Tielemans was penalised for a perceived foul – it was nothing of the sort – that the referee had initially not blown for.

And then moments after Suarez made it 2-2, the Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira flapped at Fernandes’s corner and punched the ball into his own net. Kaique’s blunder was already in motion by the time Patrick Dorgu barged into Kaique. But Marciniak was ordered to the pitch-side monitor by Piotr Lasyk, the VAR, and from there, he weakly decided Kaique had been infringed upon by Dorgu. It was a big let-off for the goalkeeper and the hosts.

To compounded United’s frustrations, they were then reduced to 10 men late on when Tielemans, who had been booked for protesting over the first disallowed goal, received a second yellow card. It means United have now had four red cards and conceded five penalties in their last five games and, four weeks shy of Christmas, are still searching for a win on the road.

The irony was that, amidst the chaos, there was a lot Pochettino will have liked about the performance. It was far from perfect but United at least had a structure, coherence and confidence about them for long periods. But for Lammens’s shocker and some dubious refereeing, United would surely have claimed just a fourth win this season.

The problem with this United side is they never seem too far away from an act of self-sabotage. Pochettino insisted on the eve of this game that his team were not fragile, but that assessment was challenged in the crazy 160 seconds when United conceded not one but two penalties.

In truth, they could feel hard done to by the award of the first in the 29th minute. Geny Catamo went down far too easily – and very late – after Lisandro Martínez swung out a leg. There was contact but it was of the very minimal variety. Martínez rushed off to Marciniak to remonstrate but his pleas fell on deaf ears. There was a sense of justice, then, when Lammens saved Suárez’s feeble penalty.

You would have thought that would be a confidence booster for Lammens, but in no time he had gone from hero to zero, with worse to follow.

A ball was swept in behind Noussair Mazraoui and Maximiliano Araújo gave chase. There was no need for Lammens to come careering out of goal but that is what he did. When he clumsily blocked off Araújo in the process, Marciniak wasted little time brandishing a yellow card and pointing to the spot. This time Suárez made no mistake from 12 yards.

What will please Pochettino is United did not crumble again from there. In fact, they rallied and would soon be nursing a sense of injustice for the second time in four days.

Already outraged by the circumstances around Leny Yoro’s rescinded red card against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, Pochettino now had to contend with some perverse refereeing from Marciniak.

Tielemans had slipped a pass through to Amad Diallo, with his momentum carrying him into Gonçalo Inácio. Marciniak did not blow his whistle, presumably because in the moment he did not feel a foul had been committed. But after Diallo’s shot was saved and a split second before the Ivorian headed the rebound into the net, the Polish referee blew his whistle.

It's hard to know why this was ruled out 🤯 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Pat8nzJiVW

Tielemans could not believe what he was seeing and, to add insult to injury, was booked for his protestations.

The problem for United was that, because Marciniak had blown moments before Diallo put the ball into the net, VAR were powerless to review the decision.

After the match, Pochettino claimed United were punished by the referee’s decisions.

The Argentine was again in a state disbelief at some refereeing decisions, even though he appeared at pains not to land himself in hot water with Uefa.

“It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions,” Pochettino said.

On the foul awarded against Tielemans, he added: “I think everyone knows all that was… impossible [to understand]. You know, it’s difficult to understand why that happened on the field.”

What Pochettino demanded was a strong start after the interval, and he got just that. A third penalty award of the night this time went United’s way. Martínez, who had been operating as an inverted left-back for much of the game, wriggled his way past Eduardo Quaresma before being bundled over from behind by the Sporting defender. Fernandes stepped up and coolly converted the penalty. This time it was Sporting’s turn to implode, even if Fernandes and United’s goal had some good fortune about it.

Fernandes was running to the right when he cut back inside, just outside the penalty area, and struck a speculative left-foot shot at Kaique. There appeared no obvious danger and then the ball seemed to hit a divot in the ground, seemingly created moments earlier by Fernandes as he slid in, and cannoned upwards. The Sporting goalkeeper was thrown by it and the next thing the ball was flying through his hands.

A much better United performance, undermined by a terrible night for their goalkeeper Senne Lammens, who conceded a penalty and dropped a simple cross when they had a second-half lead.

Before that, there were hints of a Pochettino team in United’s football: they were industrious, energetic and fully committed, and they were the better of two limited teams for long chunks.

This is the first time United have conceded two penalties in a Champions League match since 1998.

United in the game, but things not clicking in the final third and they are not benefitting from any rub of the green.

Catamo with dancing feet in the area, and the referee decides Lisandro Martinez has tripped him. It was a belated fall and minimal contact, but I suspect it will be sufficient for VAR to confirm the decision. There was a stretch of the leg towards the player from Martinez.

I was under the misapprehension that Peter Schmeichel and Michael Laudrup were Euro 92-winning team-mates with Denmark, but in fact Laudrup had a three-year hiatus from the national team and opted to stay away from the tournament when Denmark replaced Yugoslavia. One more in the win column for the Ewing Theory (that says teams can improve without their star player).

Laudrup told FourFourTwo: “As we weren’t able to qualify, I decided to focus 100 per cent on Barça. Yugoslavia went on to win the group, but because of the war, Denmark were suddenly given their place. People asked me if I wanted to go, but I didn’t want to join at the last moment, even though I could have. I felt it wouldn’t have been fair.”

Shaun Derry, the former Crystal Palace and QPR player, is in attendance to cheer on son Jesse who is on loan at Sporting from Chelsea. Heck of a loan move for a 19-year-old, and good to see him in fine fettle after that horrible head injury he suffered on his full Premier League debut season.

“Of course, minutes have been minimal for Jesse, but nights like this you can’t beat,” Derry said. “There are some great young players that he is learning alongside.”

“He wasn’t making his bed a year ago, now he has to cook his own dinner and get himself to training.”

Wandering around the Jose Alvalade Stadium before kick-off and Cristiano Ronaldo’s face and old No 7 is pasted on the outside of the building.

How Pochettino would love a prime Ronaldo in his team but we’re in as very different era now to the one when United went into this competition with a firm expectation of winning it. It’s two wins and two defeats so far in the Champions League for United this season although you suspect they’d be happy to come away from here with a point.

They have yet to win away from home this season and Sporting, who have won three of their four European games, are third in the Portuguese league. Watch out for Colombia striker Luis Suarez and Italy midfielder Issa Doumbia, who have six goals between them in the Champions League this term.

Harry Maguire comes in for Matthijs de Ligt, who was abysmal against Liverpool, and Noussair Mazraoui replaces Diogo Dalot. Amad Diallo is in over Patrick Dorgu. Mainoo and Tielemans have struggled as a partnership all season but Pochettino again persists with that midfield pairing with Bruno Fernandes ahead of them.

They need to finish 24th or higher to avoid elimination. They only have two fewer points (after four games) in the Champions League than they do in the Premier League (after 11).

Few Manchester United fans expected a positive result from Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge at Anfield, but the bar will not be set so low for Sporting in the Champions League this evening.

The manner of the 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, even accounting for Leny Yoro’s early red card, was dispiriting but not unexpected. The next few weeks will reveal how Pochettino intends to get a grip on the job.

When it comes to United’s Champions League prospects, the comeback win over Roma at the tail-end of Michael Carrick’s tenure made their position less perilous, but avoiding outright elimination is the first target.

United are 19th in the table, with the top 24 teams going through. Those between ninth and 24th go into a play-off round before the last 16. After Sporting away, United host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before a trip to Villarreal so there are stiff tests to come.

Sporting are well-placed after three wins from four, but their Champions League schedule is rather one-sided: in their final three matches they travel to Roma, before playing Barcelona and Manchester City. They reached the quarter-finals of the competition last season, losing narrowly to Arsenal over two legs.

They are third in their league, having been weakened by the summer sales of Geovany Quenda (to Chelsea), Morten Hjulmand (to Atletico Madrid) and Ousmane Diomande (to Nottingham Forest). The vast majority of goals are scored by Colombian striker Luis Suárez.

Bruno Fernandes, United’s captain, returns to his former club tonight and there is hope Luke Shaw could be back at left-back. Pochettino must decide whether or not to stick with Matthijs de Ligt, who was extremely rusty at Anfield but may need the minutes.

Yoro’s one-game suspension was overturned by the FA, and he would have been available for this one in any case.

Arsenal have a plethora of options in defence, with one out-of-favour star linked with a departure

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Arsenal could lose a first-team defender who has fallen out of favour with manager Mikel Arteta.

The Gunners boast arguably the best backline in Europe at the moment, having conceded the fewest goals in the Premier League this term (just seven), and goalkeeper David Raya has already kept seven clean sheets in 11 fixtures.

Part of Arsenal's strength at the back is in their depth – but that could be seriously impacted with interest in a star who hasn't been getting in the team as much of late.

Following a back injury at the 2026 World Cup to William Saliba, the Gunners moved to bring in quality cover in the shape of England international Ezri Konsa.

Konsa has been an instant hit at the Emirates Stadium, and with Arteta now boasting eight senior players competing for places – Konsa, Saliba, Gabriel and Cristhian Mosquera in the centre, with full-backs Jurrien Timber, Ben White, Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie all capable in the middle, too – the problem is giving each of them playing time.

Sport Witness have now relayed a report from L’Interista that claims Inter Milan are interested in Mosquera, who started the Gunners' first three games of the season in all competitions but hasn't featured much of late.

The Spaniard filled in for Saliba before the Konsa deal was completed, but went off injured against Aston Villa in the second league game of the campaign, paving the way for Konsa to make his debut.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The 29-year-old has kept his place alongside Gabriel ever since – and despite Saliba returning to fitness and featuring on the bench recently, the former Villa star has remained a mainstay of the team.

This has left Mosquera out in the cold as the fourth-choice, and though the ex-Valencia man can play across the backline, White and Timber have rotated for the right-back slot, while Calafiori and Hincapie have shared left-back, leaving him with very few minutes since the start of the campaign.

Mosquera only signed last summer, but with ESPN reporting the transfer fee to be just £13 million, Arsenal may well consider flipping the 22-year-old for a steep profit, with the report claiming Arsenal want around £30m for his signature.

The champions also have a homegrown talent in the form of Marli Salmon, still just 17 years old but having already impressed both centrally and at right-back.

FourFourTwo understands that Arsenal have no interest in selling Mosquera in January but could reassess the situation next summer.

Mosquera is worth €40 million, according to Transfermarkt. Arsenal host Manchester City this weekend when Premier League action resumes.

#873. Dominic Calvert-Lewin signs new Leeds deal

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The England international has extended his stay with the club until 2029

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal, taking his stay with the club until 2029.

The England international joined Leeds on a three-year deal after leaving Everton as a free agent in 2025, and has now extended for another two and a half years.

He scored 15 goals in all competitions last season and so far has six in this campaign, having rebooted his career following a difficult spell marred by injuries at Everton, and earned a recall to the England squad.

Leeds said: “Leeds United are delighted to announce Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract with the club.

“The England international has put pen to paper on a two-and-a-half-year deal at Elland Road, keeping him in West Yorkshire until the summer of 2029.

“Everyone at Leeds United is thrilled Dominic has signed a new deal and we look forward to seeing him continue to impress in the famous white shirt.”

Calvert-Lewin has started all 11 top-flight fixtures of this season and scored in the statement 4-1 victory over Chelsea on Saturday. Leeds currently sit seventh in the Premier League, four points off the Champions League places.

He won the Premier League’s Player of the Month Award in December after scoring in six consecutive matches - becoming the first Leeds player to win the award in 24 years.

His performances were recognised by Thomas Tuchel, who called him up to international duty for a 1-1 friendly draw with Uruguay in March, and he retained his place the squad for Nations League matches against Spain and Czechia.

His latest England appearance was against Spain earlier this month when he stepped off the bench to win his 15th cap in the Three Lions’ 3-2 win.

#872. Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence

Raheem Sterling has scored 123 goals in 396 Premier League appearances and provided 65 assists

Raheem Sterling grew up a stone's throw from Wembley Stadium, and went on to start a European Championship final for England there.

At his peak, the four-time Premier League winner was earning Â£325,000 a week at Chelsea.

"Raheem is a huge player with a huge influence in the last few years in English football," said then Blues boss Thomas Tuchel when he signed a 27-year-old Sterling in a Â£50m deal in 2022.

"He is at the perfect age to take responsibility around the younger players that we have and be an example.

"He just needs to do what he did over the last few years and he will be a huge asset for us."

Sterling enjoyed a 10-year England career, also played for Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal, and commanded combined transfer fees of about Â£100m.

But his career at the top level looks to be in the balance at the age of 31 after he was handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, for dangerous driving. Sterling has also been disqualified from driving for two years and ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work.

At an earlier hearing in September, Sterling admitted dangerous driving on a motorway before crashing a Lamborghini on 28 May.

The crash caused "substantial" damage to his car and all four wheels, which prevented him from driving further, the court heard.

Sterling also admitted possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis.

How Sterling went from England star to court appearance

Sterling's life was touched by tragedy at a young age.

Born in Kingston, Jamaica, he was just two when his father was shot dead.

His mother, Nadine, was determined to give her children a safer environment to live in. She moved to England to lay a path for Sterling and his sister to join her once she had found a home and finished her education, while cleaning bathrooms and changing bedsheets in hotels to earn extra money.

Sterling grew up on a housing estate in Neasden, north-west London, and spent part of his education at Vernon House, where teachers attempted to help the football-obsessed youngster with behavioural problems.

In an interview with the Players' Tribune, external in 2018, Sterling said: "I was so naughty that they kicked me out of primary school. I just didn't like to listen to anyone but my mum. That was my problem."

He was 10 when teacher Chris Beschi told him: "If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or in prison."

Sterling would grow to become one of the standout English attacking talents of his generation.

Watch: Moment Raheem Sterling arrested after car crash

Raheem Sterling: From school struggles to a class of his own

On 14 November 2012 - aged 17 years and 342 days - Sterling made his England debut on the night his Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard won his 100th cap in a 4-2 defeat by Sweden in Stockholm.

Sterling would go on to make 81 more appearances for his country, scoring 20 goals.

He featured at three World Cups - 2014, 2018 and 2022 - and two European Championships. He was one of the standout players as England reached the Euro 2020 final at Wembley, where they were beaten by Italy.

Sterling was now at the peak of his career - the former Queens Park Rangers youngster, who has a tattoo on his forearm of a young boy holding a football looking up at the Wembley arch, named in the team of the tournament by Uefa.

Liverpool had signed a 15-year-old Sterling from QPR for Â£600,000 in February 2010.

He made his senior Reds debut two years later and became the second-youngest goalscorer in their history - behind Michael Owen - when he scored the winner against Reading in October 2012 at the age of 17.

In 2015, Sterling joined Manchester City in a deal worth up to Â£49m, making him the most expensive English player at the time.

He had been under contract at Anfield until 2017 but turned down a new deal to move to Liverpool's rivals, with City boss Manuel Pellegrini describing the 20-year-old as "one of the best attacking players in world football".

Sterling went on to score 131 goals in 339 appearances in all competitions during seven successful years at Etihad Stadium.

As well as four Premier League titles, he helped City win five League Cups, one FA Cup and one Community Shield.

It was while he was at City, in 2021, that Sterling became an MBE in the Queen's Birthday Honours for his services to racial equality in sport.

"I am grateful to have been recognised," he said. "But my priority is to try to help to educate society and myself. I'm learning every day."

After City came the move to Chelsea, where his career began to stall.

Tuchel, now England manager, was sacked two months after signing Sterling, who made just 45 Premier League starts for the Blues over four years.

Off the pitch, he launched a scholarship fund aimed at closing the gap in the number of black British students who go to university.

On the pitch, he was finding it a struggle.

He spent 18 months as a member of Chelsea's so-called 'bomb squad', and a season-long loan to Arsenal in 2024-25 proved largely unsuccessful.

Sterling: If you grew up in a certain area you feel like there's limits

As well as his success on the field, Sterling has made headlines off it too.

In 2015, when he was 20, reports began to surface about his behaviour away from the game.

Sterling was pictured apparently inhaling nitrous oxide and was also photographed smoking a shisha pipe.

That prompted then Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers to warn Sterling he would "look back in 20 years and wonder what he was doing".

Sterling also made headlines while on duty for England at the 2018 World Cup in Russia.

The Sun ran a story titled "Raheem shoots himself in the foot" as pictures emerged of a tattoo of an M16 assault rifle on his leg.

Sterling explained on social media: "When I was 2 my father died from being gunned down to death I made a promise to myself I would never touch a gun in my life time. I shoot with my right foot so it has a deeper meaning."

The incident led to a widespread discussion in the UK about the treatment of black athletes in the media, with comparisons drawn between how Sterling's life was covered compared to others.

Sterling spoke out a number of times on the issue and wider racism in society, which was reflected in him being made an MBE.

Five years after his MBE, Sterling's career has stalled. He has not played since appearing for Feyenoord on 17 May, after agreeing a short-term move to the Netherlands.

Eleven days after that game, he was arrested after crashing a Lamborghini near the M3 in Hampshire.

Watch: Sterling joins PL 100 club - best goals & stats

Listen: From Wembley schoolboy to playing for England at Wembley

Sterling was riding the crest of a wave when he moved from Manchester City to Chelsea in the summer of 2022 for Â£50m.

His medal cabinet was already fit to burst with 10 major trophies under Guardiola and, alongside Harry Kane, he was arguably England's most important player for then head coach Gareth Southgate.

Tuchel viewed Sterling as his number one target that summer and Chelsea's new ownership - Behdad Eghbali and Todd Boehly - delivered as the club entered the post-Roman Abramovich era.

Two months later, Tuchel was sacked and Graham Potter was in situ.

Sterling's career has not been the same since.

It is, of course, senseless to suggest the troubles Sterling has had on and off the pitch in recent years are simply down to the sacking of Tuchel in 2022.

But speak to those close to Sterling and they will explain Tuchel was among the key factors behind the winger's decision to swap Manchester for west London.

He was captivated by Tuchel's vision, not only for the team, but his role in it.

New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino may well be about to address the dreaded left-back problem that has hampered the club for years

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Manchester United plan to address their issues at left-back by signing a player dubbed ‘the next Riccardo Calafiori’, following another poor result away at Sporting.

The Red Devils dropped two points in Europe last night away in Lisbon, with new manager Mauricio Pochettino winless in his first two games in charge, as the scale of the task at hand becomes clear.

With Manchester United 19th in both the Premier League and the Champions League's league phase right now, Pochettino is under pressure to deliver quickly, with January earmarked for much-needed new signings.

Once again, United have struggled at left-back this season, with veteran Luke Shaw injured for much of the campaign.

Lisandro Martinez started the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino's first fixture, while Diogo Dalot has played out of position to cover there this term, with no obvious candidate to step in during Shaw's absence.

Sport Witness, however, have relayed a report from Gazzetta dello Sport, which claims that United have “already made moves” to sign Juan Miranda of Bologna.

The Spaniard signed for I Rossoblu following the sale of Riccardo Calafiori to Arsenal, and has impressed in Serie A with similar attacking instincts and reliable performances in manager Raffaele Palladino's backline.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

While Bologna are looking to tie Miranda down until 2030, there is significant interest from both Pochettino and Newcastle United, who see the 26-year-old as an option to alleviate the burden on Lewis Hall at left-back.

FourFourTwo understands that the Red Devils have a modest budget for January and may be limited in what they can do in the transfer market – meaning that cost-effective signings like Miranda may be the way forward, should Pochettino wish to strengthen.

After finishing third in the Premier League last season, manager Michael Carrick welcomed four new faces to Carrington in the form of Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans – all midfielders – and backup goalkeeper Karl Darlow, along with the returning Marcus Rashford, following his successful stint on loan with Barcelona.

While the lack of depth in defence and attack has been obvious this season though, United's midfield acquisitions have been questioned too for their lack of dynamism, with Carrick ultimately paying for the side's atrocious form with his job after just 10 league games.

United have won just three matches all season in all competitions.

Miranda is worth €15 million, according to Transfermarkt. Manchester United face Brentford this weekend when Premier League action resumes.

He has written cover features for the mag on Mikel Arteta and Martin Odegaard, and is assisted by his cat, Rosie, who has interned for the brand since lockdown.

#870. Brighton bounce back with Conference League win as Hearts suffer last-gasp defeat

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Osman scored twice and set up another for Charalampos Kostoulas in a 4-0 win

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Ibrahim Osman scored his first Brighton goals as his side returned to winning ways by cruising to a 4-0 success over 10-man Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League.

Talk of the high-flying Seagulls potentially being shock Premier League title contenders this season was dampened slightly by Sunday’s surprise 2-0 defeat at Hull.

But Brighton were back to their best against Romanian champions Craiova at the Amex Stadium, with winger Osman putting the Seagulls ahead in the third minute.

Jack Hinshelwood stepped over the ball following Ferdi Kadioglu’s low cross from the right before being played in by Charalampos Kostoulas and squaring to leave Osman with a simple tap-in.

Matt O’Riley had the ball in the net in the 27th minute but the effort was ruled out for offside against Chema Andres, but Maxim De Cuyper scored Brighton’s second six minutes later.

Things went from bad to worse for Craiova, who currently sit top of their domestic league, as defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off in the 39th minute for stamping on O’Riley’s ankle.

Osman set up Kostoulas for the third goal before quickly claiming his second with a fine individual effort as Brighton made it 10 points from four games in the competition.

The 21-year-old should have had another assist but his inviting low cross was blazed over the open goal by substitute Femi Azeez, who later curled narrowly wide.

Azeez’s glaring miss mattered little as Brighton comfortably extended their unbeaten home record to eight games ahead of attempting to put the league campaign back on track when Newcastle visit on Sunday.

Elsewhere on Thursday night Hearts’ Conference League hopes suffered a hammer blow as Folarin Balogun’s stoppage-time goal consigned them to a 3-2 defeat at home to Monaco.

Theylooked on course to pick up their second league-phase point after stunning first-half strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota either side of goals from visiting pair Folarin Balogun and Edian Diop.

But in the last of four added minutes, USA forward Balogun got himself free in the box to slot home and maintain Monaco’s perfect record in the competition.

Hearts will now require high-scoring victories over Borac and Pafos in their last two games to have a chance of scrambling into the top 24 and qualifying for the knockout phase.

Terry Venables arrived at Middlesbrough in 2000 to work alongside manager Bryan Robson in an unconventional setup

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Mark Schwarzer has revealed that he feared a difficult reunion with Terry Venables when the former Australia manager arrived at Middlesbrough – only to find that the coach was willing to put their past disagreement behind them.

The pair had fallen out over Schwarzer’s availability for international duty in 1997, when the goalkeeper chose to honour a commitment to Boro rather than join an Australia squad under Venables.

Schwarzer had reason to worry about the potential for awkwardness when Venables was appointed to work alongside Bryan Robson at the Riverside in December 2000, tasked with helping Middlesbrough to beat the drop.

Schwarzer told FourFourTwo: “I was worried when Terry came in, because his previous job had been manager of Australia.

“I’d just joined Middlesbrough when we had that League Cup semi-final at the same time as an Australia call-up.

"Terry had made it clear that if he called you up, he expected you to be there

"Bryan Robson asked him if I could stay because it was one of the biggest games in Middlesbrough’s history.”

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“Terry initially agreed, then three days beforehand called and said I had to choose. I told him I’d made a commitment to my club. He didn’t pick me again, including for the World Cup play-off against Iran.

“When he arrived at Middlesbrough, I wondered if there might be a problem. To his credit, he was brilliant. He basically said 'These things happen, let’s move on'."

Instead of allowing the dispute to linger, Schwarzer says Venables did a fantastic job of working out how to get Middlesbrough back in form

He said: “He made a huge impact at Middlesbrough. He spoke to everyone about what they thought was going wrong, then made his own mind up about how to address it.

“Terry was exceptional at not undermining Bryan. Robbo was still at the front of things but had this incredible coach to learn from. If Terry hadn’t come in, we would have been relegated.”

Boro eventually finished the 2000-01 Premier League season in 14th, well clear of the drop.

#866. Europa League match suspended after police clashes over Palestine banner

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The game, being played on neutral ground in Batumi, Georgia, was halted in the 26th minute and restarted 30 minutes later

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

The Europa League game between Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva was suspended for around 30 minutes on Thursday when police clashed with fans of the Turkish club after they displayed a banner in support of Palestine.

The game, being played on neutral ground in Batumi, Georgia, was halted in the 26th minute but restarted after the interruption.

Turkey’s Haberturk broadcaster said Georgian police used pepper spray against the Besiktas fans, who also unfurled a Palestinian flag, prompting referee referee Morten Krogh to stop the game with the score 0-0.

In a statement, Besiktas accused the Georgian security forces of using “disproportionate” force against supporters before and during the game.

Georgian police entered the stands and ⁠used pepper spray on Besiktas fans, Turkish outlet NTV reported.

“We strongly condemn the security forces for their use of disproportionate force against our fans,” the club said. “We also extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to all our fans affected by these incidents.”

The report added that Turkish fans chanted “Down with Israel” and that Besiktas players and director of football Onder Ozen spoke to supporters before play restarted to calm the situation.

The Turkish Football Federation condemned the treatment of Besiktas supporters on X, saying they were subjected to unacceptable behaviour and discrimination. It said it would press for an investigation.

The TFF’s statement read: “We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, conduct and interference directed at Beşiktaş supporters, both inside and outside the stadium, before and during our club’s UEFA Europa League match against Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Georgia.

“No practice that disregards the universal values of sport, human dignity, mutual respect and the principles of fair play, or that involves discrimination, exclusion or security failures, can be tolerated.

“Nor can there be any question of remaining silent in the face of such conduct, which endangers our supporters’ safety and targets their fundamental rights and freedoms.

“As the Turkish Football Federation, we declare unequivocally that we will follow this matter to its conclusion to ensure that the events are fully investigated, those responsible are identified and the necessary sanctions are imposed without delay.

“There must be no tolerance for covering up these events, allowing those responsible to evade accountability or permitting similar violations to recur.

“We emphasize that we stand firmly with our club, Beşiktaş, and our supporters, who faced a series of problems, particularly serious security failures, and extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to all our supporters subjected to interference and mistreatment.

“Let no one forget that we will not remain silent in the face of disrespect, discrimination and security violations directed at representatives and supporters of Turkish football.

“We will act decisively on national and international platforms to ensure that all necessary steps are taken, particularly with UEFA, and that those responsible are held accountable.”

Fenerbache also posted in support of their Turkish rivals.

The ⁠officiating team and the Besiktas players ‌left ​the pitch before ‌the game restarted.

Earlier, the Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel counterparts, the state-run Anadolu Agency reported.

Hapoel Beer-Sheva and Israel FA had not commented on the incident at the time of publishing.

#865. Wrong calls and bad results: Are refs making Man Utd's problems worse?

Man Utd have been plagued by refereeing decisions in Mauricio Pochettino's first two matches in charge against Liverpool and Sporting; United also received an apology from Pro Ref earlier this season for VAR's incorrect call in their defeat to Man City; But Utd's problems

Mauricio Pochettino will need more than just good performances to turn Manchester United’s season around – refereeing decisions will have to go their way too.

Pochettino's first two games in charge have been plagued by controversial moments, following a similar pattern during the club's dreadful start, which has left them 19th, inside the Premier League relegation zone and out of the Carabao Cup.

United's luck appeared to be changing when Bruno Fernandes' shot was deflected in off a divot against Sporting on Wednesday, but the officials in Lisbon left Pochettino furious again as Amad Diallo's equaliser late in the first half was harshly ruled out for Youri Tielemans' foul in the build-up.

"It's difficult to answer as everyone saw it was impossible [to award a foul]," said Pochettino. "It's difficult to understand why that happened on the field."

Szymon Marciniak, referee in the 2022 World Cup final, had also already blown his whistle before Amad scored despite the forward being through on goal. Tielemans was booked for the tackle and the midfielder was later sent off after receiving a second yellow.

There was more controversy when United's third goal, and what they thought could be the winner, was ruled out following a VAR check. Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched the ball into his own net at a corner, although it was disallowed for Patrick Dorgu's foul.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Pochettino had already been complaining about officials this week with Leny Yoro's one-match suspension overturned on Tuesday after the defender was shown a straight red card with the score at 0-0 in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Yoro was dismissed for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity, although it appeared striker Alexander Isak wouldn't have reached the ball had the defender not fouled him.

Refereeing chief Howard Webb still backed the officials' process on Match Officials Mic'd Up, although he was non-committal when sharing his own verdict on the incident.

Pochettino also felt Liverpool's opening goal, scored by Dominik Szoboszlai from the free-kick conceded by Yoro, should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola was standing next to the Man Utd wall when the ball was struck.

Barcola appeared to be pushed towards the United defenders by Bruno Fernandes, revealing a grey area in the laws of the game, as they do not explain that type of incident.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The most significant incident of United's season came prior to Pochettino's arrival when United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision to award Erling Haaland's winner in Manchester City's 1-0 win in September which was initially ruled offside before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu, but Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland, and Webb acknowledged the error.

In the same game, Man Utd benefited from Man City's Phil Foden being sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, a decision only narrowly backed 3-2 by the Key Match Incidents panel, while the United captain wrongly avoided a yellow card despite initiating the incident.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Yoro's red card against Liverpool wasn't the first time he has been harshly sent off for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity this season.

The defender was shown a straight red card when United trailed 1-0 at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last month and then lost 2-0.

Yoro brought down Atletico's Jonathan David, who was heading away from goal, after the pair came together just inside United's half. "It is soft! No way, that should not be a red," said Sky Sports' Clinton Morrison.

United have had some good fortune. In their only Premier League win of the season, Harry Maguire escaped punishment for a handball to put his side ahead against Ipswich.

Had the defender's shot gone straight into the net, it would have been disallowed, but because Jacob Greaves diverted the attempt in, it was allowed to stand.

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa was fined £25,000 last month over his post-match comments following their draw with United. Arbeloa felt Maguire had committed a foul shortly before United's late equaliser and that the officials had favoured the away side.

"All fouls for them," he said. "You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire, it's a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here."

And then, in a similar incident to United's third goal against Sporting, Dorgu's dramatic equaliser in United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa earlier this month was allowed to stand despite Man Utd goalkeeper Senne Lammens appearing to impede Villa keeper Zion Suzuki, who flapped at the corner and missed the ball.

Liverpool are beginning to see the very best of Florian Wirtz if recent form is anything to go by

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Florian Wirtz's £116 million Anfield arrival last summer was, on paper, a marquee addition to the Premier League, until he took to the field.

Supporters of all clubs were expectant, not least Liverpool fans. His debut campaign proved an awkward adaptation to English football, one in which the German seemed caught between systems, clearly in transition.

Fast forward to today and the player who lit up the Bundesliga with Bayer Leverkusen appears to have finally arrived on Merseyside.

Wirtz produced a standout display in Sunday’s 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United, where he scored an improvised goal to extend the Reds' lead and created 10 chances - albeit against 10 men - before finding the net again in Wednesday night’s 3-0 Champions League triumph over Club Brugge.

The underlying numbers from Gradient Sports prove this is no fleeting purple patch, either, especially after three goals in two games over the November international break.

According to Gradient Sports’ data, Wirtz’s overall player grade dipped sharply from a league-leading 91.0 in his final Bundesliga season with Leverkusen in 2024/25 to 73.1 during his debut 2025/26 Premier League campaign.

While his overall 2026/27 Premier League grade sits at 73.9, his attacking execution indicates a resurgence back toward his Leverkusen peak.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In the Premier League this season, Wirtz has had a 48 per cent increase in chances created - jumping from 1.99 to 2.94 per 90 minutes - ranking first among all Premier League wingers and attacking midfielders.

Even more telling is his cutting edge in the final third: Wirtz's passes directly leading to a half-chance have increased by 84 per cent, from 0.31 to 0.57 per 90.

His end product in front of goal tells a similar story. Gradient data notes that Wirtz’s positively graded shots have risen from 0.24 to 0.38 per 90 - closing in on the 0.45 he posted in 2024/25. Similarly, his 1.61 shots in the box per 90 actually surpasses his final Leverkusen tally of 1.60.

So, what has initiated the turnaround? New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for tweaking Wirtz's role and adjusting the team's tempo, but Anfield may also owe a debt of gratitude to Jurgen Klopp.

Since taking charge of the German national team, Klopp has turned Wirtz into his talisman; he has four goals in his last four international appearances. And it's that confidence which has bled into his club form, aided by private counsel from the former Reds manager. Wirtz revealed recently that he regularly speaks with Klopp about life at Anfield, taking on board "small, private things" from a man who knows exactly how to win over the Kop.

Armed with Klopp’s guidance and backed by the evidence of improved creative metrics in the Premier League, Liverpool’s £116m man is finally beginning to look worthy of his price tag.

#862. Alessio Russo exclusive: Staying calm is key to success as striker

England and Arsenal striker Alessia Russo speaks about football memories and handling pressure in front of goal as she partners with Lucozade

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Alessia Russo has two European Championships and a Champions League to her name and has established herself as one of England’s most prolific strikers.

In another impressive year for the 27-year-old, she became the highest-scoring English player in UEFA Women's Champions League history with a recent hat-trick against Benfica, was named England Women's Player of the Year and earned a place in the FIFPRO Women's World 11.

Speaking to former Three Lions striker Ian Wright at the launch of her new long-term partnership with Lucozade, the England and Arsenal forward discussed how she fell in love with football and the mentality behind her performances.

Russo grew up in Maidstone, Kent and football always featured in her life.

“Football has always been a massive part of my life,” she said. “Growing up, my dad would take me to watch women’s games at Charlton, and I remember looking up to those players and dreaming of doing the same one day.

“To see how far the game has come is incredible. Women’s football is now about so much more than what happens on the pitch. It’s influencing fashion, culture and bringing communities together in ways I could never have imagined growing up.

“To be part of that journey is really special.”

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Now one of the leading strikers in world football, Russo believes her calm approach is one of her biggest strengths when it comes to finding the back of the net.

"I've always been really laid back. I'm always wanting to win. Just because I'm not angry or shouting or screaming, doesn't mean I don't want to win and I don't want to score," she said.

"I think that calmness is something that I try and bring to the game. And I think as a striker, you have to be calm in and around the box. When things aren't going your way, I just kind of strip it back. I like to train hard and then whatever happens in the game happens.

"You can't control a whole lot as a No.9. You're quite reliant on other players. But what you can control is the moments that you do get."

The partnership will see Russo work with Lucozade Sport to better understand her individual hydration and fuelling requirements, with the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil on the horizon.

She will also help inform future product innovation as the brand continues its longstanding support of the Lionesses, dating back to 2006.

Ayisha Gulati is the women's football writer at FourFourTwo. Fresh from a summer covering the Lionesses’ triumphant Euro 2025 campaign in Switzerland, she brings a passion for all things WSL, UWCL, and international women’s football. She has interviewed names including Alessia Russo and Aitana Bonmati and enjoys telling stories that capture the excitement on and off the pitch.

In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

The Nature Index is a database of author affiliations and institutional relationships. The index tracks contributions to research articles published in high-quality natural-science and health-science journals, chosen based on reputation by an independent group of researchers.

The Nature Index provides absolute and fractional counts of article publication at the institutional and national level and, as such, is an indicator of global high-quality research output and collaboration. Data in the Nature Index are updated regularly, with the most recent 12 months made available under a Creative Commons licence at natureindex.com. The database is compiled by Nature Portfolio.

The Nature Index uses Count and Share to track research output. A country/territory or an institution is given a Count of 1 for each article that has at least one author from that country/territory or institution. This is the case regardless of the number of authors an article has, and it means that the same article can contribute to the Count of multiple countries/territories or institutions.

To glean a country’s, territory’s, region’s or an institution’s contribution to an article, and to ensure that they are not counted more than once, the Nature Index uses Share, a fractional count that takes into account the share of authorship on each article. The total Share available per article is 1, which is shared among all authors under the assumption that each contributed equally. For instance, an article with 10 authors means that each author receives a Share of 0.1. For authors who are affiliated with more than one institution, the author’s Share is split equally between each institution. The total Share for an institution is calculated by summing the Share for individual affiliated authors. The process is similar for countries/territories, although complicated by the fact that some institutions have overseas labs that will be counted towards host country/territory totals.

Adjusted Share accounts for the annual variation in the total number of articles in the Nature Index journals. It is arrived at by calculating the percentage difference in the total number of articles in the Index in a given year relative to the number of articles in a base year and adjusting Share values to the base year levels.

The bilateral collaboration score (CS) between two institutions A+B is the sum of each of their Shares on the papers to which both have contributed. A bilateral collaboration can be between any two institutions or countries/territories co-authoring at least one article in the journals tracked by the Nature Index.

natureindex.com users can search for specific institutions or countries and generate their own reports, ordered by Count or Share.

#859. 'Best midfielder in the world' - where does Bellingham rank?

Bellingham finished 11th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or

Is there a better central midfielder on the planet than Jude Bellingham right now?

Not according to Jose Mourinho. The Real Madrid manager might be trying to manage the Englishman's minutes, but he did not hold back in his praise after the 23-year-old came off the bench and scored a superb volley, helping Real overturn a half-time deficit to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

"He has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything," Mourinho said.

"He's an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world."

Bellingham's impressive 45-minute cameo came just nine days after an outstanding, all-action display for England in a 3-2 Nations League win in Spain.

'Extravagant, brilliant!' - Bellingham's wonder goal

While the former Birmingham and Borussia Dortmund player also earned plenty of plaudits for his displays at the 2026 World Cup, where he scored seven times, Mourinho believes Bellingham's unique blend of craft and graft isn't yet fully appreciated.

"He can play as a '10', as an '8', with two pivots, with one," Mourinho said after the win against PSV. "That's why I said, when the Ballon d'Or was discussed, that it was outrageous he wasn't among the top 10."

While wingers like Lamine Yamal or Michael Olise are also likely to be contenders for the 2027 award, is there anyone you would rather have in central midfield than Bellingham?

BBC Sport looks at what makes him so good, and who his closest challengers are.

Is Bellingham currently 'the best player in the world'?

Although only 23, Bellingham is already in his fourth year at Real Madrid and is on course for his most productive campaign since his debut season in 2023-24, when he scored 23 goals and provided 13 assists, including setting up Vinicius Jr in the Champions League final.

He has seven goals and four assists in 18 appearances this season. Only three central midfielders have more goal involvements across Europe's top five leagues, but Bellingham's all-round game is what sets him apart.

He leads his Real team-mates for possession won, duels won and fouls won. And while only Kylian Mbappe has had more shots on target, Bellingham offers far more than just late runs into the box.

He has played more passes into the final third than any other Real player, leads the club for ball carries and is second only to Arda Guler for chances created.

When Bellingham's coaches at Birmingham gave him the number 22 shirt, it reflected their belief that he could play any role, as a number 10, 8 or 4.

He has fulfilled that potential to become the complete midfielder.

While Bellingham made his senior debut with Birmingham, Vitinha also spent part of his formative years in the Midlands, scoring once in 22 appearances during a loan spell at Wolves - a spectacular long-range strike against Chorley in 2021.

But goalscoring isn't what the Portuguese playmaker is best known for - it is his metronomic passing.

The 26-year-old has played a pivotal role in Paris St-Germain's back-to-back Champions League triumphs, with manager Luis Enrique saying he "embodies the perfect midfielder".

He was named man of the match in the victory over Arsenal last season, having completed 141 of his 150 passes, matching the Champions League final record set by Barcelona's Xavi in 2011.

Vitinha finished third in the Ballon d'Or voting in 2025 but slipped to 14th this year, a ranking Luis Enrique disagreed with.

"It's a real pleasure to have a player with such physical abilities and that mentality," the PSG boss said last month. "He's at an incredible level."

Rice finished one place below Vitinha, and four below England team-mate Bellingham, in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings after helping Arsenal win their first Premier League title since 2004.

He briefly played at centre-back as a youngster at West Ham before establishing himself as a top-class defensive midfielder for the Hammers. But since joining the Gunners in 2023 he has taken his game to another level, adding significantly more attacking output.

Rice created 17 big chances in the Premier League last season, as defined by Opta, a total bettered only by Bruno Fernandes and Rayan Cherki.

The 27-year-old has also registered 14 assists in all club competitions since August 2025. While set-pieces have undoubtedly contributed to that tally, he offers much more.

He ranks among the top 4% of central midfielders across Europe's top five leagues for progressive carries, while posting similarly impressive figures for chances created, touches and expected assists.

The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner missed Spain's Nations League defeat by England this month through injury, and his absence was keenly felt as the hosts uncharacteristically struggled for control, at least against 11 men.

It was a far cry from Spain's triumphant Euro 2024 and 2026 World Cup campaigns, both of which ended with him being named player of the tournament.

The 30-year-old completed 756 passes as Spain won their second global title, the highest total ever recorded at a World Cup.

His performances this summer were all the more impressive given that he had taken time to return to his best after tearing his anterior cruciate ligament, an injury that sidelined him for most of the 2024-25 campaign.

The former Manchester City player has slotted in seamlessly since joining Barcelona in August, and averages 106 successful passes per 90 minutes in La Liga - the second-highest figure, behind Vitinha, of any player in the top five European leagues.

The student playing in La Liga: Introvert Rodri's unique rise to top

Pedri may be six years younger than Rodri, his midfield partner at the Camp Nou, but he boasts extraordinary experience for a 24-year-old, having made more than 250 appearances for Barcelona, not to mention playing at two European Championships and two World Cups.

The Tenerife-born midfielder combines tigerish work-rate with quality in possession.

He has created 26 chances from open play in La Liga this season, the sixth-highest total across Europe's top five leagues, and wins possession an average of 7.6 times per 90 minutes, the 10th-highest figure.

However, such is Spain's wealth of midfield options that he is not even guaranteed a starting place for his country, with Fabian Ruiz preferred for their final three matches at the 2026 World Cup.

Paris St-Germain midfielder Ruiz, who finished 10th in this year's Ballon d'Or rankings, also deserves to be in any debate about the world's best midfielders.

He might not yet have the profile of Barcelona team-mates Rodri or Pedri, but on current form alone, versatile youngster Lopez is one of Europe's best box-to-box goalscorers.

The 23-year-old already has nine goals and seven assists this season. Counting only goals scored in Europe's top five leagues and the Champions League, no central midfielder has more.

While Lopez can also operate on the wing, the presence of Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon means he has mainly featured as a number eight or a number 10 this term.

The Barcelona academy graduate played only a bit-part role as Spain won Euro 2024 and was unfortunate to miss the World Cup after breaking a bone in his foot in May.

However, a summer off enabled him to hit the ground running this season, and he has not looked back.

A former US international has warned that even the globe's best manager wouldn't suddenly transform the Stars and Stripes into world beaters

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Pep Guardiola has been out of work since bringing an end to a decade at Manchester City this summer – and has suggested that his next job could be in charge of a national team.

Guardiola won six Premier League titles during his time at the Etihad, before deciding to step down at the end of last season.

In an interview this week though, the Catalan indicated that he sees his next step as being “a national team”, after talks to become Italy boss during the summer.

Guardiola opted not to take the Italy job, believing at the time that he needed a break from football, but has since been linked with the USA vacancy.

Mauricio Pochettino had been in charge of the American national team since 2024, leading them to the last 16 of this summer’s World Cup, but brought his tenure to an end last week to take charge of Manchester United.

Given that Guardiola is the highest profile manager currently out of work, and is one of the greatest of all time, having previously won two Champion Leagues and three La Liga titles with Barcelona, plus three Bundesliga titles with Bayern Munich, links to the job were inevitable.

Pochettino has said he would be in favour of Guardiola succeeding him as US boss, and former American national team goalkeeper Brad Friedel, who won 82 caps for his country, also admits it would be an intriguing appointment.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

He warns though that even bringing in someone like Guardiola would not suddenly transform the national team into potential World Cup winners.

“I don’t know really what the discussions are within US soccer,” the 55-year-old told FFT, speaking in association with nye casino.

“We need the players to be able to win World Cups, and I think there's a lot to break down with that.

“Do I think Pep Guardiola is one of the best managers ever? Yes. Does that mean if you hire him that the US will win the World Cup? No. But it would be a little bit of a buzz.”

There will be more from Friedel in FourFourTwo soon.

#856. Osman stars as Brighton bounce back with Conference League win

Brighton and Hove Albion vs CS Universitatea Craiova. UEFA Conference League Round 1.

American Express StadiumAttendance: Attendance26,796.

Match report as Brighton beat 10-man Universitatea Craiova 4-0 in the Conference League; Ibrahim Osman scored his first Brighton goals in the win; Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign; Osman also set up Charalampos Kostoulas for a third

Ibrahim Osman scored his first Brighton goals as his side returned to winning ways by cruising to a 4-0 success over 10-man Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League.

Talk of the high-flying Seagulls potentially being shock Premier League title contenders this season was dampened slightly by Sunday's surprise 2-0 defeat at Hull.

Winger Osman finished a flowing move to set Albion on course to avoid a further unexpected defeat before Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign to double the lead.

Romanian champions Craiova were left with little hope of a comeback at the Amex Stadium when defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off in the 39th minute for stamping on the ankle of Matt O'Riley.

Osman set up Charalampos Kostoulas for the third goal before quickly claiming his second with a fine individual effort as Brighton made it 10 points from four games in the competition on a bitterly cold evening in Sussex.

3: GOAL! The move started with Kadioglu down the right and he then picks out Kostoulas in the box, who in turn feeds Hinshelwood in space and his low driven ball to the back post is tapped home by the unmarked Osman.

33: GOAL! Brighton double their lead as the visitors play a risky crossfield pass that is intercepted by De Cuyper, who then beats Popescu with a delightful right-footed curler from distance that leaves the 'keeper rooted to his line as the ball goes in off the post.

39: RED! The referee did not need long to look at that, with Screciu shown a straight red for that dangerous-looking tackle on O'Riley.

46: SAVE! Azeez, with his first touch since coming on, whips a lovely ball in from the right and Hinshelwood must have thought he had scored with a bullet header - but Popescu responds with a brilliant save.

61: GOAL! Osman feeds Kostoulas in the area and from a tight angle, the Greek's low drive beats Popescu at his near post.

78: CLOSE! Azeez twists and turns on the right edge of the box, but his curler is inches away from finding the top corner with the 'keeper motionless.

#855. Jojo Siwa Teases Baby Plans With Boyfriend Chris Hughes

Jojo Siwa, who’s been dating boyfriend Chris Hughes for over a year, revealed her hope that her next major chapter includes becoming a mom and having a baby.

It takes two to tango, but Jojo Siwa is looking toward bigger dance numbers.

Over a year and a half after the Dance Moms alum found love with Love Island UK’s Chris Hughes, she revealed she’s ready to become a dance mom of her own.

As revealed during the Nov. 25 episode of the Petticoat Revolution podcast, her ideal next chapter would be to “have a baby. Be a mom. That’s my next thing.”

And the 23-year-old is more than ready to hit pause on her professional career in the meantime.

“Obviously that's not a career thing, but like a life thing,” she explained. “Like career, career is doing her thing. She’s always there. She's been there for 15 years. She'll keep going, she'll keep being there.”

But this is not the first time Siwa has envisioned a long future with Hughes, who she met while filming Celebrity Big Brother in the UK in the spring of 2025.

n fact, Siwa previously revealed she puts her daydreams into practice when it comes to Hughes one day getting down on one knee.

“He got me this ring for Christmas last year,” Siwa told E! News of the jewelry she wore on her right hand in an interview alongside her boyfriend in October. "I wear this every day, I’ve never taken it off—sometimes I'll switch it to my other hand just see what it feels like.”

And while the 33-year-old admitted that Siwa’s trial run with an engagement ring was news to him, the revelation brought a smile to his face.

“I didn't know she did that, but now I do,” he said. “It's kind of cute.”

But sometimes, Siwa revealed, she shimmies a bit too close to the engagement sun for someone who lives so squarely in the public eye.

“I'll forget that I've done it,” she said of wearing her ring on that finger. “And I'm like, ‘Oh crap, it's been there too long. Someone's going to get a photo or something.’”

Though the couple both confirmed there aren’t any immediate plans for wedding bells to be ringing, Hughes affirmed, “One day, of course.”

As Siwa put it, “We're in a very happy phase of life right now.”

For a deeper look at Siwa and Hughes' romance, keep reading...

The couple's whirlwind romance unfolded for the whole world to see during their appearance on Celebrity Big Brother.

A year later, Siwa—who split from ex Kath Ebbs following her time on the U.K. the series—released the song "Serendipity" in honor of the now-couple's chance encounter.

"The only word to explain what happened on this day a year ago… Serendipity," Siwa wrote in an Instagram post. "Today, I’m reminded of the moment that quietly changed everything."

Less than a month after they put their bond on display in the Big Brother house and emphasizing they were just friends, Hughes and Siwa confirmed they were dating in late May 2025.

At the time, Siwa cheekily nodded at the romance during a cover of "Bette Davis Eyes" at one of her shows, in which she instead sang "Chris Hughes' eyes."

The Love Island alum joined Siwa at several stops of her Infinity Heart Tour, which spanned across Europe, the U.K. and the United States. In a sweet glimpse at their backstage moments, Siwa added of the tour in an Instagram post, "The show represents who I want to be as a person and the artist that I wanna be in this lifetime, and it’s translated so well to the crowd."

Siwa and Hughes stepped out for their first red carpet as a couple at the Dancers Against Cancer's 2025 Gala of the Stars in Beverly Hills, California.

Siwa shared a glimpse into the couple's favorite bonding activity: golfing in a sweet Instagram photo dump of her summertime adventures.

In September 2026, Hughes gave his followers a slice of life moment by filming Siwa arriving to his place in England—and naturally they shared a sweet embrace to boot.

October 2026: Coming Back Like a Boomerang

Siwa and Hughes turned the Gala of the Stars into a date night two years in a row by attending again in 2026.

Siwa proved her love for Hughes knows no bounds by teasing her next big step in life was to become a mom.

"That’s my next thing," Siwa teased during a Nov. 2026 appearance on the Petticoat Revolution podcast. "Career is doing her thing. She’s always there. She's been there for 15 years. She'll keep going, she'll keep being there.”
