Spurs are getting things moving in the right direction under Roberto De Zerbi - but there's a missing piece to the puzzle

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Tottenham Hotspur’s resurgence under Roberto De Zerbi has breathed fresh life into the club after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.

There is one clear deficiency in their current make-up that threatens to limit what they can achieve in 2026/27, though - they can't finish.

Despite sitting comfortably in the top half after 12 games, Spurs’ underlying attacking numbers tell the story of a side creating plenty and squandering too much of it.

Tottenham have rattled off 170 shots in the Premier League this season - the fifth-highest tally in the division - while only Liverpool and Manchester City have registered more efforts from inside the penalty area than Spurs’ 109.

But, when it comes to actually hitting the target, De Zerbi’s side slump to 14th across the top flight.

There's also an issue with their ball-striking. According to Gradient Sports’ analysts, just six of Spurs’ 170 league attempts have been graded as ‘unsaveable’ - a figure bettered by every team in the Premier League bar Everton (5).

For context, high-flying Brighton have racked up 20 unsaveable efforts, while Erling Haaland has managed seven on his own. At 3.5 per cent, Tottenham boast the lowest proportion of unsaveable shots in the entire division.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

A glance at De Zerbi’s attacking options explains why to some extent. Richarlison has been frozen out entirely and is angling for a January move, Dominic Solanke has managed just two league goals, and big-money summer arrival Omar Marmoush is yet to hit the ground running in north London.

Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke is the team's joint-top Premier League goalscorer with two goals after 12 matches: Spurs need a centre-forward in January.

Enter Real Sociedad’s 22-year-old Icelandic international Orri Oskarsson.

Oskarsson is by no means LaLiga’s most prolific frontman, having netted four times in the Spanish top flight this term but his underlying metrics point towards a striker ready to thrive in a possession-heavy, attack-minded system.

Unlike De Zerbi’s Spurs, Real Sociedad do not dominate the ball as often, leaving their striker without service for large periods of matches. Oskarsson, though, is making every second count when his team are in possession, averaging a goal every 64 minutes that La Real actually have the ball this season.

In total, he has scored nine times across his last 13 appearances for club and country.

What makes Oskarsson particularly suited to Tottenham is how intelligently he moves to receive the ball. Gradient Sports’ data shows the Icelandic forward receives line-breaking passes 45 per cent of the time, placing him among LaLiga’s best at peeling off defenders and making himself available to creative midfielders.

That off-the-ball awareness is reinforced by the fact he has received the ball in a clear shooting position 10 times in the league this season - a tally bettered only by Barcelona’s Raphinha (13) and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (11).

Once the ball arrives at his feet, Oskarsson has the penalty-box nous Tottenham lack. Ninety-two per cent of his LaLiga shots this season have been taken from inside the box, which aligns nicely with the 109 close-range openings Spurs have already generated this term. Even more impressive, out of the 25 shots he has taken in LaLiga, five have been graded as unsaveable by Gradient's analysts - just one fewer than Tottenham’s entire squad combined.

Gradient have also flagged just one occasion all season where Oskarsson opted to shoot when passing to a better-placed teammate was the superior option, highlighting good judgement under pressure and decision-making that is rare for a 22-year-old.

Meanwhile, his Expected Goals (xG) ranks sixth-highest in LaLiga - a decent return given Real Sociedad’s modest share of possession and chance creation.

And best of all, a winter deal is entirely plausible. For a Tottenham side creating plenty of penalty-box opportunities but with nobody reliable to tuck them away, Oskarsson could be one of the more shrewd January investments the market has to offer.

#853. SFA to deliver revised proposal after young player vote delayed

The Scottish FA will continue to consult with SPFL clubs about youth development after initial plans failed to reach a member vote.

At a summit in September, Scottish football's governing body proposed financial incentives and penalties along with quotas, in a bid to get more homegrown talent playing for Scottish clubs.

Initially, the plans were to have been voted on at an SFA general meeting in October and the SPFL's annual meeting this month.

But the SFA are now aiming to put refreshed proposals to the clubs early in the new year, with the plan to implement them for the start of the 2027-28 season.

Despite being "encouraged", the governing body added that "recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation."

"The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews," a Scottish FA statement read.

"We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game."

"It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

At their initial consultation with clubs, the SFA put forward three proposals:

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Scottish Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Premier Sports Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Clubs should field Scotland-eligible Under-21 players for an average of 60 minutes in each game across all four SPFL divisions

#851. Sarah Michelle Gellar Reveals Her, Freddie Prinze Jr.'s Holiday Plans

For Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr.’s family, holidays reign supreme and Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is must-see TV, she told E! while detailing her partnership with Ancestry.

Sarah Michelle Gellar knows the best way to slay the holiday season.

And for the Buffy the Vampire Slayer and husband Freddie Prinze Jr., it all comes down to focusing on their community—a tradition that dates back to her own childhood.

“A lot of times for Christmas and New Year's, we're traveling, so Thanksgiving is something that's always been important to be at home for,” Gellar told E! News in an exclusive interview. “When I was younger my mom always used to open our apartment to anyone that couldn't afford to go home or didn't have family. So, we do the same. We're actually having probably one of the largest Thanksgivings we've had in a couple years this year.”

That said, there is plenty of quiet family time amid the busy day with guests. And it’s those traditions with kids Charlotte, 17, and Rocky, 14, that have stood the test of time. In fact, Gellar admitted that when it comes to their family holiday traditions, “what's funny is they haven't really evolved” as the kids have gotten older.

“I grew up in New York City, so Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is obviously very important,” Gellar noted. “I used to go the night before and watch them blow up all the floats—you'd sit there and you'd bring your thermos of hot chocolate because it'd be freezing, and you'd watch. And so I've grown up with that parade, and I, from the time my kids were born, I'm like, we will be watching this parade."

In fact, a pre-Thanksgiving work trip to New York City was enough to have her eldest wondering if their favorite tradition might be put on pause. “When my daughter was knew I was leaving, she's like, ‘You're going to be back for the parade, right?’” Gellar revealed. “I'm like, ‘The parade's on Thanksgiving. I will be home. You don't have to worry.’ So, the Thanksgiving Day grade is always like a really big a big one for us.”

Plus, there’s the sprint to get the decorations up—and wind down with a movie marathon. On the docket this year is Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and checking out Ariana Grande in Focker-in-Law.

“Getting a tree up is always that weekend,” she explained. “Also for us going to the movies like that weekend because it's always a great movie weekend. So we've already got our tickets. We got our tickets for to see Hunger Games. We have our tickets ready to go to see Ariana in Fockers. We're ready to go."

But one tradition that never gets old for the Prinze family is taking the time to give back.

“I didn't grow up with a lot,” the Cruel Intentions actress shared. “I had a single mom, and we did the best we could. But my mom always wanted to remind me to be grateful for my situation because there are children that were so much less fortunate. So we used to every year go to the post office and get a secret Santa.”

And it wound up being a formative experience. “Even at a young age, I clocked that these kids weren't asking for the Cabbage Patch Kid that I wanted,” Gellar recalled. “They were asking for shoes that didn't have holes in them or a jacket that fit—that first realization that there's real need out there and that you can make a difference. And even though you know we couldn't, I wanted to fill every Christmas list that was there, and my mom would have to explain to me like we can do as many as we can within reason.”

She added, “But just being a part of making that child's Christmas or that family's Christmas, they ask for diapers, they ask for these things, and so that sort of always stuck with me.”

In fact, she’s continued to pay it forward, teaming up with Ancestry for its Gathering the Good initiative, inspiring people to take a peek at the history of giving in their own life while also helping those in need this holiday season.

The spirit of giving is also a trait she and Prinze are passing on to their teens.

“I just love watching the joy that it brings to my kids to be able to see that they can make a difference in someone's life," she noted. "I want someone to always remember there's always something you can do. And you know maybe it's not financial, maybe it's giving your time.”

Put simply, “There's so much you can do to make someone else's life a little bit easier, and in turn, it makes your life easier because you're just that little bit happier.”

For a look back at Gellar and Prinze's sweetest memories with their kids, keep reading...

Driving home the fact that son Rocky looks just like dad Freddie Prinze Jr., Sarah Michelle Gellar shared a photo from a "race weekend with my boys" in October 2026.

The actress celebrated the aspiring F1 driver completing another lap around the sun and turning 14. "I should have known from your speedy delivery, the excitement you would bring," she wrote on Instagram in September 2026. "You have no idea how lucky I feel to watch you chase your dream. You inspire not just me, but everyone around you."

Sarah also paid tribute to her "best friend" and daughter Charlotte, who was born three years and one day prior to her little brother."I’m not sure how you are 17 already," the Buffy the Vampire Slayer star shared on Instagram in September 2026. "You may have been the child that made me a mom, but now you are the person that brings out the best in me. (Not to mention my biggest champion) Thank you… for being you."

Not switching gears, Rocky's mom shared a heartfelt post when he turned 13."Aside from being one of the fastest in the state, you are one of the most polite, kind and funny kids I know," she penned on Instagram in September 2025. "I can’t believe you are a teenager. I love you more than my words can express!!!"

As the sun set on an old year and rose on a new, Sarah, Freddie and the kids enjoyed a trip to Hawaii—with her posting a "vacation dump" in January 2024.

Fans know what this crew did that summer. The I Know What You Did Last Summer costars took their children on a trip to Italy in July 2023.

Sarah's intentions for this adorable throwback? To celebrate Rocky's birthday!"Your laugh is infectious, your jokes are the best and your spirit is … EVERYTHING," the Cruel Intentions alum raved on Instagram in September 2023. "You make every day brighter."

Making a rare red carpet appearance, Charlotte joined her mom at the L.A. screening of Sarah's movie Do Revenge in September 2022.

Scooby-Dooby-Doo, where are you? The Scooby-Doo costars and their children returned to Hawaii to say goodbye to 2021 and hello to 2022.

For Charlotte's birthday in 2021, Sarah reflected on how "this day 12 years ago my greatest life truly began."

And on Rocky's 9th birthday that year, the Ringer celeb looked back at when he was born and his parents' "hearts exploded."

This 2019 photo of Charlotte starting fourth grade and Rocky beginning first is one for the books.

Sarah gave a shout-out to her husband on Father's Day 2016."The greatest part of every day is watching life through my children's eyes," she wrote on Instagram, "so today (and every day) Freddie I thank you."

After Charlotte was cast as baby Simba in a children's production of The Lion King, her mom shared a snap of her using Freddie's binder to study lines."So no matter how hard we have tried (and believe me we have tried) to convince our daughter to find any hobby but performing, she has shown a great love (and talent) for being on the stage," Sarah wrote on Instagram in 2016 before joking, "(wonder where she gets that from?)."

"In my household cooking is family time, time to #unplug and connect," the cookbook author wrote on Instagram in 2015 alongside a photo of her and her little ones. "I treasure these moments."

#850. The Portuguese second-tier team hosting Celtic in Europe

Portuguese second-tier side Torreense have not played top-flight football since the 1991-92 campaign, but are making their debut in the Europa League this season

S.C.U Torreense's league fixtures this season include meetings with the 'B' teams of Sporting, Benfica and Porto.

But the Portuguese second division club, located 35 miles north of Lisbon, are in this season's Europa League after stunning giants Sporting to win the Taca de Portugal in May.

"This is a landmark moment," Andre Sabino, the club's director of football and CEO told BBC Sport.

Torreense had never played a European home match before their 2-1 defeat by Sunderland in October and welcome Celtic to Leiria on Thursday (20:00 GMT).

They won at Norwegian side Lillestrom on their debut but lost heavily in Hungary against Ferencvaros before beating Ararat-Armenia last time out.

Managed by Luis Tralhao, whose brother Joao is an assistant to Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid, the club are hoping to do more than just make up the numbers.

"It is something extraordinary for Torreense. These are clubs with huge histories, strong identities and enormous European experience," Sabino added.

"To be able to share the same competition and compete against them is a privilege. But we don't want to simply participate. We want to compete."

Torreense captain and Cape Verde international Stopira (pictured above) scored a penalty in extra time as his side beat Sporting 2-1 in the Taca de Portugal final earlier this year

Second-tier Beira-Mar played in the 1999-2000 Uefa Cup, although they were a top-flight team at the time of qualifying. But Torreense are the first team from the second division to qualify by winning the Taca de Portugal.

"The Portuguese Cup has been played since 1938 in its current model and it was the first time that a second division team won it," Portuguese football journalist and ex-Benfica goalkeeper Jose Delgado told BBC Sport.

"You can imagine when they could defeat a giant club like Sporting in the final, it was quite a surprise and for the city, it's something very, very special."

After beating Lillestrom, they have already exceeded the expectations of some. "I thought that Torreense could go through the Europa League with no points," added Delgado.

With Portugal ranked outside Uefa's top five leagues, every club in the Champions League, Europa League or Conference League has a responsibility to perform well to earn their nation important ranking points.

"For Portuguese football, everybody [thought it] was nice that a club like Torreense won the cup but also we had some concerns," said Delgado.

"The first game everybody thought that Torreense had no chance against Lillestrom and they won. It was quite a good surprise. But it's like a fairytale for Torreense because they are a small club."

Torreense's Estadio Manuel Marques has a capacity smaller than 45 of the 48 clubs in England's sixth tier

As their 2,431-capacity home at Estadio Manuel Marques does not pass Uefa's stadium criteria, they will instead face Celtic almost 47 miles away at the Municipal Stadium in Leiria.

"Obviously, it is not ideal," Sabino explained. "Playing at home should mean playing in your own stadium, in front of your own supporters and in the environment that represents your club.

"But at the same time, we understand the logistical and regulatory requirements involved in European competition.

"We have to look at the bigger picture. We are extremely grateful for the opportunity to compete in the Europa League and we will make Leiria feel as much like home as possible."

The additional travel has not deterred supporters from watching their beloved club face big European names.

"Our supporters and our people are what make a home, regardless of the kilometres. The response from our supporters has been fantastic," Sabino added.

"They understand that this is a historic moment for Torreense and they want to experience it with us.

"We hope to see Leiria filled with Torreense colours and feel that support from the first minute."

Torreense pocketed 630,000 euros (Â£533,000) for their win over Lillestrom

Torreense missed out on a return to Portugal's top division for the first time since 1991-92 after a 2-0 two-legged defeat by Casa Pia in a promotion/relegation play-off in May. And fell at the first hurdle in their defence of the Taca de Portugal.

But qualification for the Europa League's league phase guarantees a financial injection of at least 5m euros (Â£4.2m).

Every positive result and extra round reached adds more to that pot.

"For a club like Torreense, it is a very significant amount," Sabino explained. "It gives us an opportunity to strengthen the club in several areas and to accelerate projects that otherwise would naturally take much longer.

"However, we have to be very responsible. Success can create opportunities but it also creates responsibilities.

"Our objective is not simply to spend more because we have more resources. We want to invest intelligently, strengthen the structure of the club and create conditions for sustainable growth."

Torreense played competitively against Sporting's main and 'B' teams last season, something they will also do this year against Porto

Torreense have made 19 new signings from across the globe for this season.

As well as turning to Portugal's top flight for five new recruits, other signings have come from France, Greece, Spain, Serbia, Portugal, Brazil, Denmark, Morocco and Germany. The majority from outside those countries' top leagues.

Of their 32-man senior squad, just four are Portuguese.

"It has been a very different challenge," Sabino explained. "European football changes the perception of the club and naturally makes Torreense more attractive to certain players, but it also increases expectations."

Last season, Torreense missed out on automatic promotion on goal difference before losing the play-off. This term they have won only two of their opening 10 league games and sit 13th.

With the overwhelming majority of football fans in Portugal supporting one of the 'big three' of Porto, Benfica and Sporting - Delgado says sometimes home fans even cheer for their more illustrious opponents when they visit.

"Right now I think that there is a great sympathy about Torreense, but I don't think they will get many more [fans] because of this presence," he added.

"Maybe this presence will make some investors look at them in a different way and put some money in the club."

#849. Hemmings unfazed by rise at Villa and eager to take next step

Sky Sports sits down with Aston Villa prospect George Hemmings to discuss his rise to the first team; Hemmings started for seven games before an injury curtailed progress; watch Ipswich vs Aston Villa live on Saturday Night Football, kick-off 5.30pm

Football Journalist @PatrickRoweSky

Two days after being thrown into a cauldron in Istanbul during Aston Villa's loss to Galatasaray in the Champions League, George Hemmings strolls into the media centre at Bodymoor Heath, sliders on, looking entirely at home in the senior surroundings that should be new to him.

The nineteen-year-old is quiet and reserved to start but soon settled into proceedings when quizzed on that atmosphere and what the experience was like.

"It was mad," he says with a smile on his face. "When we had the ball, you couldn't hear anything but whistling."

The mentality to take to an occasion such as that is largely expected by prospects in the modern game. A lofty standard set by the likes of Max Dowman and Rio Ngumoha.

But it does not mean we should lose sight of it.

For comparison, the journalist typing this was pulling on the ASDA shirt at the same age.

Hemmings, meanwhile, has been fast-tracked into the senior squad at Villa, thrust into an industry where the scrutiny and pressure is unmatched, and has impressed in the early stages of his career.

Unai Emery has an eye for talent and a knack for helping prospects tap into their potential. He wouldn't provide the platform for Hemmings if he didn't see something in the versatile midfielder.

"He is really good with me. He is always just looking for the best and always trying to improve me," he says when asked about the guidance Emery offers.

A quick glance out the window and you can see his team-mate, Taylor Harwood-Bellis, leaving. But it is two chairs and a spotlight for Hemmings, rather than an early exit.

His answers are short and snappy. A young prospect still getting to grips with the added responsibilities that come with being a Premier League footballer. But just like on the pitch, he takes it in his stride.

I move the conversation onto his quick rise into the first team. Following a summer of change at Villa Park, where Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and more all departed, Hemmings was a shock inclusion in the starting line-up against Brighton on the opening day of the season.

A chastening 4-0 defeat would follow at the Amex Stadium, but in the brief spells of positive play from 10-man Villa on that day, Hemmings showed the flashes of talent that have caught the eye of Emery since day one.

He went on to start all seven games to begin 2026/27 before a knee injury curtailed his progress, with a first goal for the senior side still eluding him. He is yet to start a game since returning but Villa have reaffirmed their belief in the player after he penned a new five-year deal at the club.

"I am excited! It is five years, so I have a long time to improve myself and improve my game." I then pose the question of where he may see himself in his career in five years' time, where he adds: "We will have to see! I just have to keep working."

It is clear he is firmly in the plans of Emery and also revealed conversations about a potential loan exit before the season began never occurred.

"I always look at what is best for my career and once I saw that I could get a few games, I was always going to stay," he continued.

The 2-1 win against Coventry, arguably his strongest performance in a Villa shirt so far, offered a glimpse into what Emery is trying to coerce out of the young talent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Tammy Abraham's opener at the CBS Arena came courtesy of a moment of real quality from Hemmings. His perfectly placed pass with the outside of his right boot dissected Premier League opposition and made the finish easy for his team-mate.

It offered an insight into the quality Villa hope he can one day produce regularly. But the celebrations also outlined why he is in the perfect environment for that necessary development.

Abraham quickly pointed to Hemmings and embraced his team-mate. Captain John McGinn arrived with a tap on the head, with Ross Barkley and Ibrahim Mbaye following suit.

The next opportunity to impress arrives on Saturday as Villa face Ipswich, live on Sky Sports, with a six-game winless run looming over the squad.

Hemmings was already around the squad prior to the major changes that occurred over the summer. Should he continue his current trajectory, he could become an increasingly important part of Emery's plans for years to come.

At 19, he still has plenty to learn but if his early steps in senior football are anything to go by, he is unlikely to be overawed by whatever the game can throw at him. It was a short encounter with Hemmings - but you can see why he is rated so highly at the club.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Panini have launched their latest Barclays Women's Super League sticker collection, featuring teams from WSL and WSL 2 for a second year running.

This is only the fourth edition of the book for the top women’s league in this country, and Rachel Daly believes the culture of sticker collecting can play its part in growing the women’s game.

As the latest collection was launched in London this week, the ex-Lioness spoke to FourFourTwo about the rise of the women's game.

Speaking at the launch, Daly reflected on her own childhood memories of collecting Panini stickers.

"For me, it goes back to my childhood,” Daly told FourFourTwo. “I collected them with my brother. We used to, every Saturday morning, go and get the stickers.

"You'd get your piles and you'd trade them and swap them at school. Just that whole feeling of sitting down and putting stickers in.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"I'm a Leeds fan, so I always wanted to get the whole Leeds team immediately when I was younger.

"I would literally swap any of my stickers, even if I'd already got the Leeds player, just to have more.”

While Daly grew up collecting men’s players, this WSL collection offers an opportunity to introduce more fans to the women's game, something Daly believes is particularly important as the league continues to grow.

The latest album has 545 stickers across all 26 WSL and WSL2 clubs, giving fans access to collect stickers of their favourite players from across the top two tiers of English women’s football.

"The visibility of the game is massive," she added.

"For the fact that it's WSL 1 and 2, I think it's equally as important. Those players in the WSL 2 deserve the same recognition as us.

"Being able to see kids being exposed to seeing the women's game as well, it's exciting."

Daly was speaking at the launch of the Panini Barclays Women's Super League Official Sticker Collection 2027 in London. The collection is available now at retailers nationwide and online via Panini.co.uk.

She has interviewed names including Alessia Russo and Aitana Bonmati and enjoys telling stories that capture the excitement on and off the pitch.

#846. The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

South Africa’s health officials at the launch in June of lenacapavir, a drug that provides strong protection against HIV when administered twice a year.Credit: Per-Anders Pettersson/Getty

Earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment. Twice-yearly injections of this game-changing medicine — originally developed by the company Gilead Sciences in Foster City, California — have been shown to be more than 95% effective at preventing HIV acquisition1. At the same time, as Nature reports in a News feature, an HIV vaccine — that would ultimately be a more robust solution to preventing HIV — is closer than ever before.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies

In 2024, Gilead signed licensing agreements with six pharmaceutical companies, allowing them to make and sell generic versions of lenacapavir in 120 low- and middle-income countries, subject to regulatory approval. The recent FDA approval brings access a step closer in these countries. The cost to users has been set at US$40 per year, fuelling hopes that the drug will help to bring the global HIV epidemic under control.

These welcome developments contrast with the situation of public funding for HIV research and treatment, which is reeling from deep and unconscionable cuts from the US government. Many of the researchers whom Nature spoke to for the News feature had been funded by a programme for preclinical HIV-vaccine research run by the US National Institutes of Health (NIH). But the agency ended the programme last year, forcing researchers to scale back their research and seek alternative funding. Whatever funding comes next is likely to be less stable and less predictable than the NIH funding. It’s imperative that the cuts be reversed — or new government funding sources found.

The path to an HIV vaccine has been long and bumpy, with decades of high-profile and costly failures, but there is now light at the end of the tunnel. The latest strategy — known as germline targeting — is designed to trigger the production of rare, highly potent antibodies that can prevent infection with diverse HIV strains. The technique has shown encouraging results in animal models2–4 and in early trials in humans5. Researchers are more optimistic than they’ve been in years that an effective HIV vaccine could be on the horizon.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now

But in the meantime, antiretroviral drugs such as lenacapavir look poised to have a big impact on infection prevention. In Africa alone, new infections could be cut by around one-third if just 5% of adults most likely to acquire HIV received the drug, and by half if it was given to one-fifth of adults, according to the Gates Foundation’s Institute for Disease Modelling in Seattle, Washington.

But lenacapavir alone is unlikely to bring the HIV epidemic fully under control. There are several reasons for this: first, it’s not always easy to determine who needs the drug most. Second, to be effective, the drug must be taken for most of someone’s life — or at least while they are sexually active. Third, even $40 a year is unaffordable for people on the very lowest incomes.

Until recently, the United States was the stand-out funder for antiretroviral drugs for people living with HIV in low-and middle-income countries. That stopped in January 2025, when the US administration suspended funding. Although it later restored a limited amount, the effects have been devastating. A survey published earlier this year found that some 1,700 facilities previously offering treatments to people living with HIV had closed as a result (see go.nature.com/4a7ftp4).

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Such instability highlights the importance of vaccines. “The funding cuts that happened in the past couple of years have really made it even more obvious how fragile that system of reliance” on drug access is, says Penny Moore, a virologist at South Africa’s National Institute for Communicable Disease in Johannesburg. And that fragility, as Rogier Sanders, an HIV-vaccine researcher at Amsterdam University Medical Centre, says, is why research into a vaccine remains a priority: “A vaccine makes you independent from access to drugs.”

But the US cuts have not only curtailed the preclinical vaccine programme, they have also forced the postponement and scaling back of an HIV vaccine trial in South Africa. They have also affected supporting research, such as surveillance efforts tracking HIV evolution in African countries, says Nairobi-based Vincent Muturi-Kioi, who is leading development of HIV vaccines at the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative in New York City.

Success stories such as the repurposing of lenacapavir as a preventive treatment and progress in vaccine development show the importance of investment in health. It is imperative that HIV vaccine research and deployment continues to receive support, at the same time as rolling out lenacapavir as widely as possible.

It could take more than a decade to translate the encouraging results with germline targeting into an effective HIV vaccine, and the current strategy might encounter more hurdles.

The world is closer than it has ever been to an effective HIV vaccine and has a drug capable of preventing infections. Now is the time for funders to ramp up investment, not cut it back.

#845. Russell: I found Verstappen comments amusing

George Russell's long-standing feud with Max Verstappen reignited at the Las Vegas GP after the pair collided in final practice; watch the Qatar GP on Sky Sports F1 this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

George Russell says he was "amused" by Max Verstappen’s criticism of him after their feud reignited at the Las Vegas Grand Prix but admits it was "avoidable".

After colliding on track in final practice last weekend, Russell publicly criticised Verstappen following the incident. The Dutchman won the race after an intense battle between them and said afterwards that the Mercedes driver is "far below my level".

The pair have clashed several times on track in the past, most notably engaging in a remarkable war of words following an incident during qualifying at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix where Verstappen felt Russell had pushed unreasonably hard for him to be penalised.

Speaking on Thursday - back at the Lusail International Circuit almost exactly two years on from that incident - ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, Russell said: "At the end of the day, I guess I stand by what I said after practice.

"But he was the one who went out and won the race. I didn't and I'm sure he had a bit of a laugh about that, and that was reasonably amusing. From my side, just a new race weekend, try and focus on the driving and move on."

Russell was pressed on the saga throughout the FIA press conference and revealed he was perhaps "guilty of being just too open and honest when I speak with you guys [the media]".

"It's all avoidable at the end of the day, and it's all a bit unnecessary. It's not something I'm looking to continue. I'm not looking to have poor relationships with people. That's just not really the type of person I am," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"There are lessons just to be taken away from these situations. Maybe I am just too open and honest with the media because I feel that I'm having more of an open conversation with you guys as opposed to remembering there's a camera.

"There are more people in this room than there are cameras, and I feel like I'm talking to you, but I'm not actually talking to you. I need to remind myself that I'm talking to the camera there that's broadcasting to millions of people. That's the biggest takeaway."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Verstappen did not want to make any further comments about his Russell feud during his media sessions at the Lusail International Circuit.

"Everything else that has been said off track has been said. There's nothing else to add," he said.

Russell had been battling with Verstappen for the lead during most of the Las Vegas Grand Prix as a combination of a big slipstream effect and the new 2026 power units created a peloton-style race.

However, the Mercedes driver was third with three laps to go behind Verstappen and team-mate Kimi Antonelli, so went for a move on the latter at Turn 5 but crashed and eventually finished ninth.

Verstappen, who is likely to finish second in the Drivers' Championship this season, said it was "fantastic" when he saw Russell in the wall.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Russell said: "I don't think it's important to have a good relationship or no relationship in that regard to be honest. We're all fighting for race wins. My mistake in Vegas came when I was trying to overtake my team-mate.

"The truth is, my risk dial is probably a bit too great at the moment, because I'm just kind of wanting to go for these big results and get some highlights on the board towards the end of the season.

"If that was race one of the season, there's no way I would have gone for that move with two laps remaining. But two races to go in the season, I kind of wanted to go for it.

"I think the majority of us respect one another out there, and we have hard and good battles. and even the race with Max until that point was good and fair. It was very strategic."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Russell reiterated that he respects Verstappen "immensely for his driving talent and everything he's achieved on track" and feels he does not have to be friends with the four-time world champion.

"At the end of the day, we're all competitors out there. I think there's no right or wrong way about the mentality that everybody has, and I think we're all different in many regards, and you don't need to agree with one another," he said.

"I'm not looking to be best mates with anybody on the grid. I'm just working and looking and fighting to win. Simple as that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

McLaren's Lando Norris, who has fought Verstappen on track several times in recent years, agrees with Russell.

"You don't have to get on. Do you get on with everyone?" he said.

"It's just normal. It happens in life; not everyone agrees with everything. It's also a sport where you want to prove that you're better than everyone else.

"You can either do your talking on the track or you can do your talking in front of a camera. It normally always helps when you can back it up on track, that's what everyone, at the end of the day, really cares about, but I still respect both drivers a lot.

"Obviously, Max has proved to everyone [what] he's capable of and George is kind of still I think yet to prove what he's capable of. I still think he can achieve a lot in his Formula 1 career and look forward to seeing that. He's obviously had a tough year but I still believe he can have a good season and I look forward to more times when he's giving a good fight to Max."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Verstappen's former Red Bull team-mate Pierre Gasly half-joked he is "sitting and eating my popcorn and laughing" about the Verstappen-Russell spat.

"I think it was best with Max just to tell him right up in his face! He's someone that just takes anything," said the Alpine driver.

"You can have opinions, etcetera. I like both of them, obviously [they are] very different. We all know each other, we know each other since we were kids. It's not the first time, it's not the last time, these two are going to go at it."

#844. Travis Kelce Teases NFL Future After 100th Game at Arrowhead Stadium

Travis Kelce addressed his plans on returning for another NFL season with the Kansas City Chiefs following his historic 100th home game at Arrowhead Stadium.

Travis Kelce is not ready to say so long, Arrowhead.

After the Kansas City Chiefs tight end marked his 100th regular season home game on Nov. 22, he teased his NFL future while addressing his post-game pledge of “cheers to 100 more.”

“You’re not gonna play a f--kin’ 100 more games. What are you talkin’ about?” his brother Jason Kelce joked on the Nov. 25 episode of their New Heights podcast, calling out Travis. “What are you talkin’ about?”

“Yeah, you’re right, I won’t,” Travis replied. “But cheers to 100 more.”

He hinted that his final huddle may not be on the horizon. As the 36-year-old—who married Taylor Swift in July—put it, “Who knows how many I’ll get to?”

But when his older brother asked him if he was “confirming” he’ll be returning for another season, Travis paused and sighed, before replying, “No. I’m not confirming it.”

And though the athlete—who has played for the Chiefs throughout his 14 seasons in the NFL and signed a two-year contract in 2024—is keeping his football future under wraps for now, he’s continuing to celebrate his historic game at Arrowhead Stadium last weekend.

“One hundred games, dude, it feels pretty awesome right now,” Travis shared. “To think about that legacy of that stadium and it’s pretty crazy to think they’re moving on from that stadium, because of all the history that’s happened over the years and history of the franchise and everything.”

And though the Chiefs will be leaving the stadium in 2031, Travis’ memories at Arrowhead go beyond football. After all, it’s where his romance with Taylor began after he attended her Eras Tour concert at the venue in 2023.

“It’s been home for me for 14 years,” Travis expressed. “It’s been one of my favorite places to go to play and to watch not only football, but musical events and I’ve had so much history and so many things that mean so much to me happen at Arrowhead that a 100 games, it’s pretty awesome to hit that milestone.”

But that wasn’t the NFL star’s only achievement during Nov. 22 face-off against the Arizona Cardinals as Travis scored a touchdown in the first quarter, officially putting him into the third-place slot for most career touchdowns by a tight end.

And his loved ones were there cheering him on, with Taylor celebrating the exciting moment with Travis’ niece Wyatt Kelce, the eldest daughter of Jason and his wife Kylie Kelce’s four kids.

In fact, not only has Grammy winner established herself as quite the cheer captain, but she’s become “fully engulfed” in the sport, according to her husband.

“Now she knows everything,” Travis shared on a September episode of New Heights. “She sees the flags coming in, like, ‘Oh, that might be a defensive hold.’ [I’m] like, ‘What’d you say, sweetie?’ She’s like, ‘That’s encroachment.’ I’m like, ‘You know what that is?’”

For a closer look at the couple’s touchdown-worthy romance, keep reading…

Long before Taylor Swift's attendance at the Kansas City Chief's Sept. 24, 2023 game became one of the definitive pop culture moments of the year, Travis Kelce was an admirer of the Grammy winner.

The star tight end's interest in Taylor was first revealed by one of his teammates in a TikTok video posted by the Chiefs in August 2023 (which, in hindsight, was when the pair were secretly dating).

Before Travis could answer the prompt of who his celebrity crush was, wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling spilled, "Taylor Swift!"

Travis smiled at the camera before holding his finger up to his mustache, saying, "Alright now!"

Plus, Travis was just one of many celebs to attend Taylor's record-breaking Eras Tour even before the now-engaged duo kicked off their romance. But more on that enchanting moment in a bit...

No. 2: He's Not Her Usual Type (on Paper)

While he does have that daydream look in his eyes (especially when he sees Taylor on the big-screen at one of his games), Travis stands out a bit when you look back at Taylor’s dating history.

She is typically attracted to creative types, including actors (Joe Alwyn, Jake Gyllenhaal, Taylor Lautner and Tom Hiddleston) and musicians (Calvin Harris, John Mayer, Harry Styles and, most recently, Matty Healy).

But perhaps that’s why her romance with the lighthearted and cheeky athlete—who signed an updated two-year deal with the Chiefs worth $34.25 million in 2024—feels like such a refreshing option for Taylor after her six-year uber-private relationship with Joe came to an end in April 2023.

Looks like the 10-time Pro Bowler’s wishes came true after he all but manifested his romance with the superstar through sheer will, determination and declarations of infatuation.

Travis publicly aired his failed attempt to shoot his shot and talk to Taylor when he attended the Kansas City stop on her Eras Tour July 7, 2023. As it turns out, he had a special gift for her: A friendship bracelet bearing his "number" that he hoped to give Taylor. (He wouldn't definitively say if it was his jersey number or phone number.)

Despite his claim that he was "disappointed" he failed to meet her after the concert, Taylor confirmed to TIME in December 2023 that she belatedly caught his podcast pass.

"Travis very adorably put me on blast on his podcast, which I thought was metal as hell," she recalled. "We started hanging out right after that. So we actually had a significant amount of time that no one knew, which I'm grateful for, because we got to get to know each other."

So, that whole theory about the Sept. 24 game being their first official hang? As Taylor clarified to TIME, "We would never be psychotic enough to hard launch a first date."

Since dating Travis, Taylor has been seen in public more frequently, including outings with friends in NYC and jubilant appearances at award shows, like the 2023 MTV VMAs and the 2024 Grammys.

But her most talked-about appearance? Sitting in Travis' suite at the Chief's Sept. 24, 2023 home game against the Chicago Bears.

Rather than shy away from the attention, Taylor cheered and screamed "Let's f--king go!" when Travis scored a touchdown. Like the public, even Travis admitted he was caught off-guard by Taylor accepting his invite.

"Shoutout to Taylor for pulling up, that was pretty ballsy," Travis said days later on his New Heights podcast. "I just thought it was awesome how everyone in the suite had nothing but great things to say about her, the friends and family."

"She looked amazing," he added. " It was definitely a game I will remember, that's for damn sure."

Since then, Taylor and Travis have been photographed hand-in-hand on dates all around the world and have made multiple visits to a Christmas bar in Kansas City, where they were not shy about PDA.

And, after revealing to TIME that she retreated from the spotlight when Kim Kardashian's infamous leaked phone call in 2016, Taylor is going out tonight...and every night, if she wants to, thank you very much.

"Life is short," she said. "Have adventures. Me locking myself away in my house for a lot of years—I’ll never get that time back. I’m more trusting now than I was six years ago.”

While Travis isn't afraid to spill some tea on his Sept. 27, 2023 podcast regarding his interactions with Taylor, he still expressed his boundaries about addressing his personal life moving forward.

"I know I brought all this attention to me," he explained. "I did the whole friendship bracelet thing and told everyone how butthurt I was that I didn't get to meet Taylor." However, he continued, he didn't plan to give a full play-by-play of their relationship.

"What's real is that it is my personal life and I want to respect both of our lives," he explained. "I'm enjoying life and I sure as hell enjoyed this weekend. So everything moving forward, I think me talking about sports and saying 'alright nah' will have to be where I keep it."

He doubled-down on his desire to play it cool in a November 2023 interview with the Wall Street Journal.

"Everybody around me telling me: Don't f--k this up! And me sitting here saying: Yeah—got it," he told the outlet, before addressing the media attention. "That was the biggest thing to me: make sure I don't say anything that would push Taylor away."

But that doesn't mean he's been able to resist publicly talking about his girlfriend—crediting her for the boost in sales of his jersey and calling her "amazing" after she was booed by New England Patriots fans at a December 2023 game.

"I've never been a man of words," he admitted to WSJ. "Being around her, seeing how smart Taylor is, has been f--king mind-blowing. I'm learning every day."

Like Taylor, who is close with her parents, particularly her mother Andrea, Travis hails from a tight-knit fam, including his parents Ed and Donna Kelce.

Donna became a beloved public figure as the first mother to have two sons playing against each other in a Super Bowl, when Travis faced off against his older brother, Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce, in the big game in February 2023.

"For all the stars to align and for them to get through high school and college and the pros. And for them to both play in the Pro Bowl and to play in the Super Bowl, and then for this to happen," Donna told ET at the time. "This is just like a dream come true. I can't express enough how special this is for the family and it's just crazy."

Donna, who was married to Ed for 25 years before they divorced, supported both of her sons by wearing a half-black, half-red Eagles and Chiefs jacket.

After the Super Bowl, which saw the Chiefs best the Eagles, Travis and Jason got emotional while reflecting on sharing the experience with Donna.

"The moment I saw mom is when I got really emotional," Jason said on the brothers' New Heights podcast. "It was so awesome...She was on top of the world for a week."

"She was the heavyweight champ man," Travis added. "She was on top of it, and she shined the whole time."

Like Taylor and her younger brother Austin Swift, Travis has a special bond with his older brother Jason, who inspired him to play football.

In addition to their impressive careers as NFL players, Travis and Jason launched their podcast New Heights in September 2022, a project that has only strengthened their relationship (and their bank accounts).

"What this did was gave us a scheduled two to three hour window where we have to talk to each other and we have to talk about what we're going through, throughout the week and throughout the games," Travis told NBC Sports in February 2023. "It's almost been like therapy, man."

Sure, the pair technically never met until 2023, but there have been a few invisible strings tying them together.

Taylor and Travis both count Miles Teller as a friend, with the Top Gun: Maverick star and his wife Keleigh Sperry even being recruited by Taylor to star in the music video for "I Bet You Think About Me" off Red (Taylor's Version) in 2021.

Travis, meanwhile, joined Miles and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes for golfing practice ahead of the American Century Championship in 2022.

Miles tweeted a photo of himself on the golf course with the athletes, writing, "Grip it and rip it." Travis proved the bromance was real when he reposted the shot and added, "Back at it like we never left!!"

(Interestingly enough, Miles is a noted diehard Philadelphia Eagles fans, so perhaps he put in a word with Jason to broker an IRL meet-up between Travis and Taylor?)

While Taylor attended the Sept. 24, 2023 game solo, she brought an entourage of celebrity friends with her when she attended the Chiefs' match-up against the New York Jets at New Jersey's Metlife Stadium on Oct. 1.

She was accompanied by BFFs Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds and his friend Hugh Jackman, as well as Sophie Turner, Sabrina Carpenter and Queer Eye's Antoni Porowski.

While their attendance at the game spoke volumes, even more telling was Ryan following Travis on Instagram.

Not only has Travis played in four Super Bowls, winning three of them (NBD!), but he's also hosted Saturday Night Live, so you know he can handle intense spotlight with ease.

That may seem trivial, but Taylor has penned several songs regarding her fear that her level of fame could prove to be too much for her romantic partner to handle. (See: "Peace" and "The Archer.")

"It all depends who you're with," Taylor said in, "If they have a serious issue with it, I guess you'll hide or whatever, but I don't really like that, because it makes me feel like I'm running from the law or something. I don't want to feel like a fugitive, like, 'Oh my god, we're having a relationship, better hide!'

"I feel like if you can be in a relationship and have it seem normal, that would be good."

And in his WSJ interview, Travis proved he's more than ready for the pressure that comes with being married to someone as powerful as Taylor.

"Obviously I've never dated anyone with that kind of aura about them...I've never dealt with it," he said. "But at the same time, I'm not running away from any of it."

"The scrutiny she gets, how much she has a magnifying glass on her, every single day, paparazzi outside her house, outside every restaurant she goes to, after every flight she gets off, and she's just living, enjoying life," he added. "When she acts like that I better not be the one acting all strange."

Further proving their love is worthy of a rom-com treatment, fans were swooning after a concertgoer captured video of Taylor running into Travis' arms and exchanging a passionate kiss after performing in Argentina in November 2023. And that was after she changed the lyrics in Karma from "the guy on the screen" to "the guy on the Chiefs," much to Travis' surprise as he attended alongside her father, Scott Swift.

Turning out for one another's stadium takeovers—Taylor attended 13 Chiefs games her first season with Travis, traveling straight from her Tokyo show to make the Super Bowl—is a show of how serious their relationship is.

"I'm going to see him do what he loves, we're showing up for each other, other people are there and we don't care," Taylor told TIME of their public support. "The opposite of that is you have to go to an extreme amount of effort to make sure no one knows that you're seeing someone. And we're just proud of each other."

And if her presence at the NFL games annoys you, well, Taylor can't even be bothered to have bad blood with you.

"There's a camera, like, a half-mile away, and you don't know where it is, and you have no idea when the camera is putting you in the broadcast, so I don't know if I'm being shown 17 times or once," she said. "I'm just there to support Travis. I have no awareness of if I'm being shown too much and pissing off a few dads, Brads, and Chads."

Travis was born in—are you ready for it?—1989. Screaming, crying, throwing up, etc.

Speaking of Killa Trav's birthday, which falls on October 5, did you know he shares his with Taylor's late grandmother Marjorie Finlay, the subject of her song "Marjorie" off of 2020's evermore? If we didn't know better, we'd think this is a sign...

She's loved him three summers now, honey, and she's going to get 'em all.

#843. More ref frustration as Pochettino's chaotic start at Man Utd continues

Three pens and a red as Man Utd draw against Sporting

Two games, no wins. Two red cards, two goals scored. One goal disallowed, six conceded. Is it possible for Mauricio Pochettino to have learned anything from a chaotic first week as Manchester United boss?

United and Pochettino went on the warpath before the Champions League encounter with Sporting, furious at Leny Yoro's dismissal at Liverpool which they believe was unjust and shaped the eventual 4-0 defeat.

Club officials were seething after the 2-2 draw in Lisbon as well.

This time it was 2022 World Cup final referee Szymon Marciniak in the firing line. Blowing before Amad's first-half header went into the net meant VAR had no chance to assess whether the Polish official was right to rule Youri Tielemans had fouled Goncalo Inacio before prodding the ball through to the Ivorian.

Former United winger Ashley Young didn't think so. He called Marciniak's performance "a disgrace".

That Tielemans picked up a booking that eventually led to his late red card - meaning the Belgian will miss the home match with RB Leipzig on 8 December just compounded the situation. United have now had four players sent off in their past five games.

Then, in a matter of minutes, Marciniak decided neither Manchester United keeper Senne Lammens nor Sporting counterpart Kaique had been fouled as they conceded. Their respective defences complained bitterly. Marciniak was only asked to go to the pitchside monitor by VAR for the latter incident, which he overturned.

United insiders felt the Tielemans incident was clearly not a foul and Amad's goal should have stood. They also felt any foul on Kaique by Patrick Dorgu was marginal and did not warrant their goal being disallowed.

Pochettino trod a fine path, knowing if he said something too controversial, it could land him with a fine.

A nod of a head in agreement was his initial reaction in his post-match news conference, when asked if he felt Marciniak had got it wrong.

A few minutes earlier, he had been more expansive when he spoke to TNT.

"It's difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game," he said. "We were punished a lot in key actions."

Divots, howlers and bad decisions - dissecting Man Utd's draw in Lisbon

Four goals, chaos and controversy - Man Utd held in Lisbon

Not for the first time this season, United controlled extended periods of a game they ended up not winning.

The goals they conceded at the Jose Alvalade were bizarre.

Seventy-five seconds after superbly saving one penalty, goalkeeper Lammens suffered a rush of blood and conceded another, which was scored.

Lammens was at fault for the second, when he dropped the ball into the path of Sporting striker Luis Suarez, who scored with an overhead kick.

"I think we dominated and we deserved to win the game, but we didn't for different circumstances," said Pochettino.

"All the teams make mistakes, but for these mistakes the punishment (for us) is too big in every single mistake. Many other clubs make mistakes or tilt in a different circumstance, in a more positive way. But that is in the way we are. We need to take responsibility."

United are still to win away from home in any competition this season. They have now won once in their past 13 matches. In the Champions League, they are 19th, two points in front of Roma, who are just below the top 24, which guarantees passage to the next phase.

Mauricio Pochettino asked about Amad's disallowed goal against Sporting

Young said Lammens may be one mistake from being dropped.

The Belgian's performance was not good and errors are beginning to mount.

It is not what Pochettino needs right now. United showed faith in the Belgium international this summer by bringing in 36-year-old Karl Darlow as his understudy.

Darlow did end last season as first choice at Leeds but started just 30 league games in his three seasons with the Elland Road club. Tom Heaton, 40, who was also on the bench against Sporting, has not played in a senior game since February 2023.

Could Pochettino contemplate leaving Lammens out.

"This type of thing happens," he said. "That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."

Huge Lammens blunder sees Sporting equalise

It has been a whirlwind week for Pochettino, who last Wednesday morning UK time was still United States boss.

There have been a few blows to absorb, and lessons are having to be learned quickly.

But despite the clear frustrations, the 54-year-old is glad he accepted the challenge.

"I am happy to be here," he said. "I'm so excited to be the face representing this club.

"We are here because the situation wasn't the situation all the fans and people expect. We are here to take the responsibility from one week, and we are going to improve for sure.

"It's going to be tough, of course. Nothing is easy. But we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and, most important, we have the players and the power and the energy from our fans, which is massive."

#842. Julianne Hough Shares Cryptic Trust Quote After Adrian Williams Split

After Julianne Hough and Peloton instructor Adrian Williams's breakup, the Dancing With the Stars co-host shared a cryptic message to her Instagram account about trust.

Julianne Hough is tangoing with matters of the heart.

After the Dancing With the Stars co-host revealed that she and Peloton instructor Adrian Williams had broken up, she posted a series of photos and cryptic messages to social media, putting her feelings center stage.

“The highest currency is not attention," read one image reshared to Hough's Instagram Story Nov. 25, "it's trust."

Earlier, the 38-year-old posted another text-only post to her Stories that said, “May you attract someone who pours as much love and care into you as you pour into them.”

The Emmy winner also shared a photo of herself holding her dog Sonny among the pointed messages—the same photo Williams had shared to his Instagram Stories Nov. 22 when he’d soft launched their romance on social media. Hough had reshared the photo to her own account at the time, with a source confirming their relationship to E! News the following day.

Amid the breakup, Hough—who finalized her divorce from Brooks Laich in 2022—was also busy with the Nov. 24 finale of Dancing With the Stars, sharing a photo of herself and Sonny in a bathroom mirror to her Stories that same night with the caption, “Never have the words ‘The show must go on’ Rang more true than today! Grateful for all of you incredible humans that love and show up for your people.”

As for Williams, while the fitness pro has yet to publicly comment on his brief romance with the dancer, he appears to be sticking to his own routine, keeping his focus on his fitness and his own pup, Frankie. The 42-year-old posted a photo of the dachshund during a walk to his Instagram Stories Nov. 25.

And when his split from Hough was confirmed, Williams shared his own cryptic message, reposting a photo from his motivational account that included a picture of him in his car with a text-only photo that read, “Your reset doesn’t have to make sense to anyone else. Mine has three pedals.”

For a look at more stars who have called it quits in 2026, keep reading.

The Dancing With the Stars co-host confirmed her break up with the Peloton instructor after a brief romance.

The split came just two days after Williams soft-launched his relationship with Hough on social media, sharing a photo of her holding her dog Sunny to his Instagram Stories, which she’d then reshared to her own account.

The Dancing With the Stars pro confirmed his breakup with the OnlyFans model after nearly one year of dating, telling Us Weekly on Nov. 10, "I'm single."

"We just decided to go our separate ways," he added, "and I’m taking my own time."

"We’re still friends, we’re still cool," Bueckers said during an appearance on Fudd's Fudd Around and Find Out podcast. "We broke up over a year ago, so we played an entire season together. We’re the utmost professional. We care about basketball.”

In October, multiple outlets confirmed that the eight-time Super Bowl-winning coach and former Bridgewater State University cheerleader ended their relationship in late 2025 after about four years of dating.

The Hills alum confirmed her romance with the "Whiskey and Rain" singer had ended after two years of dating.

#841. PL Predictions: How will your club fare this weekend?

Watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea, Ipswich vs Aston Villa, Crystal Palace vs Hull, Brighton vs Newcastle, Fulham vs Bournemouth, Sunderland vs Tottenham and Arsenal vs Manchester City all live on Sky Sports; play Super 6 on SUNDAY to win £1m!

Our top tipster Lewis Jones, aka Jones Knows, provides his analysis and betting insight across the Premier League.

I'm not for jumping off the Nottingham Forest bandwagon just yet.

Forest have taken just four points from their last seven Premier League games - no team has taken fewer - yet they sit sixth in the expected points table for the season.

There is a significant disconnect between performance levels and results, something that usually corrects itself over time. I'm still a firm believer that Oliver Glasner will get this talented group of players motoring up the Premier League table.

And I'm struggling to see why Chelsea should command quite so much respect from the markets.

Of the ever-present Premier League teams in 2026, only one has lost more games than Chelsea (14) and only one has conceded more goals (51).

Where has Xabi Alonso's defensive magic gone?

His invincible Bayer Leverkusen side conceded just 24 league goals across their entire title-winning campaign in 2023/24. Chelsea have shipped 20 in 11 games this season alone. There is a softness to this Chelsea team when opponents turn up the intensity and attack them directly.

Just two clean sheets in their last 27 Premier League games tells a sorry tale.

Forest have the attacking weaponry to expose those defensive deficiencies.

The 29/20 with Sky Bet for a home win makes lots of sense.

When the numbers and the theory marry up in the player fouls markets, I'm usually willing to get stuck in. And there is a lovely little match-up brewing down Leeds' right flank that Sky Bet may have underestimated.

Jayden Bogle is an all-action footballer. He's busy, aggressive and covers plenty of ground, which brings him into contact with opposition players at both ends of the pitch. That is exactly the profile of player I like to get onside in the fouls markets.

Across his last 30 games for Leeds, Bogle is averaging 1.75 fouls per 90 minutes. A solid enough starting point when assessing the 10/11 with Sky Bet for him to commit two or more fouls - but it's the opposition that really gets me excited.

Coventry's Yann Gboho is a foul-drawing maestro.

Across his last 50 appearances for Coventry and Toulouse, the tricky winger has been fouled at a rate of 2.2 per 90 minutes, winning eight fouls across his last three appearances for Coventry.

There is plenty of juice in that 10/11 considering this bet has won in four of Bogle's last five games.

There are certain footballers you want on your side when playing the cards markets. Lisandro Martinez is very much one of them.

The Argentine looks a walking accident at times for Manchester United, such is his desire to engage physically with opposition players. But throw him into a left-back role and his chances of falling foul of the referee increase significantly.

His natural instinct is to get tight and aggressive rather than stand off his opponent - as we saw with the foul he gave away in Sporting Lisbon that led to a penalty. That's a dangerous game to play against someone with the explosive qualities of Dango Ouattara.

The Brentford winger is developing quite the reputation as a card magnet for opposition defenders.

Since the start of the 25/25 season, Ouattara has drawn a card from an opponent every 199 minutes - that's 14 cards in total. Only Crysensio Summerville (118 mins per card) has a better strike-rate.

Those are impressive numbers and his directness with the ball should make for uncomfortable viewing for Martinez. Ouattara was responsible for getting Vitaliy Mykolenko booked in Monday's win over Everton, too.

The 7/2 with Sky Bet for Martinez to have his name taken looks a price worth attacking.

There is a rather large gap between perception and reality when it comes to Ipswich.

Eleven points from 11 games looks a perfectly acceptable return for a newly promoted team. But scratch beneath the surface and things look considerably more worrying.

Ipswich's expected goals supremacy figure of -0.81 per 90 minutes is the second worst in the Premier League. When assessing their performance when matches are level, that figure drops to -0.98 - the worst in the division.

Their reliance on Julio Enciso to provide attacking inspiration is another concern. Shut him down and Ipswich can become painfully predictable.

Enter Unai Emery, who is unbeaten in 10 games away from home against newly promoted opposition with Villa.

There are very few managers I'd rather have onside when backing a team to expose the obvious tactical weaknesses of an opponent. The 10/11 with Sky Bet for the away win is worth taking.

A Merseyside derby before most people have tucked into their Sunday roast? I'm not sure we're going to be treated to a feast of attacking football.

These fixtures rarely deliver in terms of goalmouth entertainment anyway, with the last 14 Merseyside derbies averaging just 2.2 goals per game. And the unusual kick-off time could further contribute to a lack of intensity, both on the pitch and in the stands.

I've dug into the numbers surrounding major English derby fixtures played at this time on a Sunday. Across the seven instances involving the north London derby, the Tyne-Wear derby and Manchester United vs Liverpool kicking off before 12.30pm, under 3.5 goals has landed every time.

It's a small sample but one that marries up nicely with the theory.

To get some juice into the price, I'm adding Alexander Isak to register a shot on target through the Bet Builder, which gets us to Evens with Sky Bet.

Isak is starting to look like the devastating centre-forward we know he can be. He's registered a shot on target in 11 of his last 12 games, including five across his last two.

One of my favourite player markets to attack with Sky Bet is foul involvements when the numbers add up. For those unfamiliar with the market, it's simply a player's fouls committed and fouls won numbers added together. It opens up plenty of opportunities when you can identify a particularly physical individual battle.

And there's one brewing between Luka Vuskovic and Will Osula.

Osula is a proper handful. He's a powerful, willing runner who relishes the physical side of being a centre-forward. Across his last 25 starts, he's averaged 2.70 foul involvements per game.

Throw into the equation a centre-back in Vuskovic who averages 2.72 foul involvements per game for Brighton since joining from Tottenham and we've got all the ingredients for a busy afternoon for the referee.

Anyone who watched Vuskovic's battle with Oliver McBurnie last weekend will know exactly where I'm coming from. It was brutal at times. Vuskovic racked up seven foul involvements as neither player was willing to give an inch.

I'd expect plenty of grappling, shirt-pulling and wrestling when these two come together. Vuskovic's foul involvements is a market worth monitoring with Sky Bet.

The new manager bounce is a rather fluffy concept. But there is some substance to it when digging into the numbers, especially when the new man in the dugout has home advantage.

Backing the home team in each of the last 30 Premier League matches where a newly appointed manager has taken charge of his first game in the competition for that club would have returned a profit of 9.04 points to level stakes, with 14 wins.

But what really got my betting juices flowing was that 10 of those 14 home wins came with a clean sheet.

Why? Well, my hypothesis is that the quickest way for a new manager to put his stamp on a team is to address their defensive structure. Thomas Frank has openly admitted that defensive organisation is high on his list of priorities at Crystal Palace.

And he could hardly have handpicked a more accommodating opponent in that regard.

I've got plenty of respect for Hull and their ability to squeeze results out of games but their attacking process remains the worst in the Premier League. They rank bottom for expected goals, big chances created and touches in the opposition box.

That makes the 5/2 with Sky Bet for Palace to win to nil a very attractive betting proposition. Frank can get the Selhurst Park faithful onside by keeping things simple.

My colleague Adam Bate wrote a fantastic piece about Fulham's man-to-man marking tactics up against Erling Haaland, offering up some huge pointers for us punters who like to dabble in the player fouls and cards markets.

Alvaro Arbeloa wants his defenders to engage, get tight and make life as uncomfortable as possible for opposition forwards, even if that means following them into areas of the pitch where centre-backs wouldn't usually venture.

Calvin Bassey is having a fantastic season playing this way. He's got the physical attributes to thrive in such a system but there is an occupational hazard attached to defending with that level of aggression. He's already picked up four yellow cards this season.

And the identity of his likely opponent here makes the 3/1 with Sky Bet for Bassey to be carded a very appealing price.

Evanilson is a master at using his body to manufacture fouls, inviting contact from defenders before rolling them. Since the start of last season, the Bournemouth striker has drawn a card from an opposition player every 267 minutes.

The Tottenham defensive revolution under Roberto De Zerbi remains one of the more fascinating developments of this Premier League season. There is a perception associated with De Zerbi's football that it will always produce chaotic matches with chances flowing at both ends.

The numbers have been telling a rather different story.

Across his time in charge of Spurs, their expected goals against figure is operating at 1.03 - a figure that ranks them second only to Arsenal over that period. That's a very impressive foundation, particularly for a team whose reputation remains associated with defensive shortcomings.

The absence of European football should increasingly become a significant advantage for Tottenham as the schedule intensifies, too.

Sunderland's attacking troubles make this a particularly attractive opportunity to exploit Spurs' defensive improvement. A Spurs win to nil has a chance at 5/2 with Sky Bet.

Stuart Pearce was in the Manchester City dugout the last time they endured a Premier League run as bad as the one they'll be on if Arsenal beat them here - one point from five games.

City have won inside 90 minutes in just one of their last seven games across all competitions and look horribly vulnerable without the ball.

Stability is proving elusive for Enzo Maresca. He's used eight different back-four combinations across City's last 10 games in all competitions, tinkering with his defensive personnel from one game to the next. Not a single clean sheet has been forthcoming and they've shipped 20 goals in that period.

Arsenal are worthy favourites but the way to inject some juice into their price is through Noni Madueke.

He's grasped the opportunity presented to him by Bukayo Saka's absence. What he did to Lewis Hall at St James' Park was particularly impressive considering the Newcastle full-back had kept Lamine Yamal relatively quiet for England just a few days earlier.

There is an explosiveness to Madueke's game that makes him capable of creating chances without Arsenal having to dominate territory or possession - something that should be particularly valuable here.

He's registered a goal or assist in three of his last four games. Combining that outcome with an Arsenal win at 15/8 with Sky Bet appeals greatly.
